title_en: ICE reports record immigration arrests, deportations since Trump White House return
title_zh: 自特朗普重返白宫以来，ICE 报告记录了移民逮捕和驱逐出境的情况
summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement says it arrested and deported more people during a recent 12-month period than at any time in its 23-year history

body_en: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement says it arrested and deported more people during a recent 12-month period than at any time in its 23-year history
WASHINGTON -- U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said Thursday that it arrested and deported more people during a recent 12-month period than at any time in its 23-year history.

ICE said it deported 483,200 people in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30, up 9% from its previous high of 442,640 in the same period a year earlier and up 78% from 271,480 in 2024, the last year of Joe Biden's presidency.
ICE arrested 474,850 people in the most recent 12-month period, roughly double the 239,890 arrests a year earlier and more than quadruple the 113,430 arrests in 2024.
ICE had not released such precise counts since President Donald Trump returned to the White House, including for 2025.

ICE said it made more than 48,000 arrests in September, ending a two-month run of record highs that reached 50,925 in August.

title_en: Colom wins Mississippi Senate race. And, White House warns Dems over future probes
title_zh: 科罗姆赢得密西西比州参议员竞选。并且，白宫警告民主党未来的调查
summary: After more than a week of counting ballots, Scott Colom has narrowly won the Mississippi Senate seat. And, the White House has sent a letter warning Democrats who plan to investigate the administration.

body_en: Up First briefing: Scott Colom; Trump; Russia-Ukraine talks; El-Sayed : NPR

Up First briefing: Scott Colom; Trump; Russia-Ukraine talks; El-Sayed After more than a week of counting ballots, Scott Colom has narrowly won the Mississippi Senate seat. And, the White House has sent a letter warning Democrats who plan to investigate the administration.
Your support helps make our show possible and unlocks access to our sponsor-free feed.
Colom Wins Mississippi, Trump Warns Incoming Democrats, Russia-Ukraine Talks

Democrat Scott Colom has won the U.S. Senate seat from Mississippi , defeating Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by just a few thousand votes. Colom will be the first Black Senator from the state in nearly 150 years . His win expands the Democratic majority in the new Congress to 55 seats. The Alaska race is still undecided.
Scott Colom speaks with attendees at an event held at the Two Mississippi Museums in Jackson, Miss. on Aug. 1, 2026. Sarah Warnock/AP hide caption

🎧 Colom's win highlights growing voter concerns about affordability and the impact of the war in Iran, Elise Catrion Gregg of the Gulf States Newsroom and Mississippi Public Broadcasting tells Up First . During her campaign, Hyde-Smith relied on her record and President Trump's support, which Gregg says is no longer a winning strategy . This race signals a potential national shift, showing that the South is becoming a viable target for Democrats, Gregg says.

➡️ A U.S. Supreme Court ruling this year weakened the Voting Rights Act , raising the possibility of a record drop in Black Congressional representation. The Democratic blue wave lessened the expected decline, but an NPR analysis shows that Black representation in the U.S. House is still slated to decrease with the incoming Congress.

The White House is warning Democrats that their planned investigations into administration officials could cross the line into "blatant criminality." White House Counsel Will Scharf said in a letter to Rep. Robert Garcia, who is expected to lead the House Oversight Committee next year, that the administration is monitoring "abusive and capricious threats" from Democrats. The letter concludes by saying that "the administration will not be extorted and will not be cowed by unlawful process, motivated by animus, pettiness, hatred or any other unlawful motive to intimidate, penalize or interfere with the lawful functioning of government." Garcia said Democrats will not be deterred by threats from the Department of Justice or Trump's lawyers.

🎧 The administration's arguments may buy time and push Democrats to go to court to enforce their subpoenas, NPR's Tamara Keith says. She adds that the White House letter gives a preview of the legal arguments the administration might use next year. But more importantly, Keith says that it signals that the White House and Justice Department won't accept congressional investigations and oversight without a fight.

Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a significant prisoner swap after two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi. Trump's envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff are now in Moscow today to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and attempt to make more headway to end the war in Ukraine.

🎧 NPR's Charles Maynes says that, going into the talks in Abu Dhabi, U.S. officials were exploring Article 5-like guarantees for Ukraine, similar to NATO's collective security defense. A move like this would be significant if implemented , but Moscow has already rejected the concept of a "NATO lite" status for Ukraine and its full NATO membership. Kushner said that, in Moscow, he aims to brief Putin directly and persuade him to involve Europeans in discussions about European security. European leaders, concerned about potential deals made without their input, are expected to join Kushner and Witkoff after these talks, when they'll meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Ireland.
Abdul El-Sayed sits down for an NPR Newsmakers interview. Bronson Arcuri/NPR hide caption

Abdul El-Sayed has made history as the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. The 42-year-old progressive from Michigan is already calling for a new direction for his party and urging President Trump to collaborate on actionable solutions. El-Sayed said that voters have temporarily entrusted Democrats with power, but warns that they risk losing that trust if they don't act boldly. As the senator-elect comes into the new role, he is advocating for new Democratic leadership in Congress, an end to the war in Iran, the passage of "Medicare for All" and the abolishment of ICE. While he acknowledges the challenge Senate Democrats face with a majority that's a few seats shy of being filibuster-proof, he remains open to working with his new Republican colleagues. In conversation with Morning Edition 's Leila Fadel, El-Sayed reflects on the recent elections, the future of the Democratic Party and the need for impactful legislation in the upcoming years.

The average price for a new vehicle in the U.S. has hit a record high of $51,109, according to Kelley Blue Book. This figure is about $500 above the previous record set in December 2025. For years, car prices have remained high, primarily due to supply chain issues stemming from the pandemic. But there's some good news: While that new high sets a record, it only represents a 2.1% increase over the past year. This means the price is rising more slowly. 科洛姆赢得密西西比州，特朗普警告即将上任的民主党人，俄罗斯-乌克兰会谈
民主党人斯科特·科洛姆以几千票击败共和党参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯，赢得了密西西比州的美国参议院席位。科罗姆将成为近 150 年来第一位来自该州的黑人参议员。他的胜利使民主党在新国会中的多数席位扩大到 55 个。阿拉斯加的比赛仍悬而未决。
斯科特·科洛姆 (Scott Colom) 于 2026 年 8 月 1 日在密西西比州杰克逊两座博物馆举行的活动中与与会者交谈。莎拉·沃诺克/美联社 隐藏标题栏
海湾国家新闻室和密西西比州公共广播公司的埃莉斯·卡特里恩·格雷格 (Elise Catrion Gregg) 告诉《Up First》，科罗姆的胜利突显了选民对负担能力和伊朗战争影响日益增长的担忧。在竞选期间，海德·史密斯依靠自己的记录和特朗普总统的支持，格雷格表示这不再是制胜策略。格雷格说，这场竞选标志着潜在的全国性转变，表明南方正在成为民主党的可行目标。
➡️美国最高法院今年的一项裁决削弱了投票权法案，增加了黑人国会代表人数创纪录下降的可能性。民主党的蓝色浪潮减轻了预期的下降，但美国公共广播电台的分析显示，随着国会的上届，美国众议院的黑人代表人数仍将减少。

白宫警告民主党人，他们计划对政府官员进行的调查可能会跨越“公然犯罪”的界限。白宫法律顾问威尔·沙夫在给明年将领导众议院监督委员会的众议员罗伯特·加西亚的一封信中表示，政府正在监视来自民主党的“滥用和反复无常的威胁”。信中最后表示，“政府不会因敌意、狭隘、仇恨或任何其他非法动机而受到勒索，也不会被非法程序吓倒，从而恐吓、惩罚或干扰政府的合法运作。”加西亚表示，民主党不会被司法部或特朗普律师的威胁吓倒。
NPR 的塔玛拉·基思 (Tamara Keith) 表示，政府的论点可能会赢得时间，并促使民主党人上法庭执行传票。她补充说，白宫的信函预览了政府明年可能使用的法律论据。但更重要的是，基思表示，这表明白宫和司法部不会不战而屈人之兵地接受国会的调查和监督。
在美国斡旋的阿布扎比​​举行两天会谈后，俄罗斯和乌克兰同意进行重大囚犯交换。特朗普的特使贾里德·库什纳和史蒂夫·威特科夫今天在莫斯科会见俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京，并试图在结束乌克兰战争方面取得更多进展。

🎧 NPR 的查尔斯·梅恩斯 (Charles Maynes) 表示，在阿布扎比举行会谈时，美国官员正在探索对乌克兰提供类似第 5 条的保障，类似于北约的集体安全防御。如果实施的话，这样的举措将意义重大，但莫斯科已经拒绝了乌克兰及其正式北约成员的“北约精简”地位的概念。库什纳表示，在莫斯科，他的目标是直接向普京通报情况，并说服他让欧洲人参与有关欧洲安全的讨论。欧洲领导人担心在没有他们参与的情况下达成的潜在协议，预计将在这些会谈后加入库什纳和维特科夫的行列，届时他们将在爱尔兰会见乌克兰总统泽连斯基。

阿卜杜勒·赛义德创造了历史，成为第一位当选美国参议院的穆斯林。这位来自密歇根州的 42 岁进步人士已经在呼吁为他的政党制定新的方向，并敦促特朗普总统合作制定可行的解决方案。埃尔-赛义德表示，选民暂时将权力托付给民主党，但他警告说，如果他们不大胆采取行动，他们就有可能失去这种信任。随着这位当选参议员就任新角色，他主张在国会建立新的民主党领导层、结束伊朗战争、通过“全民医疗保险”以及废除 ICE。虽然他承认参议院民主党面临着多数席位的挑战，距离阻止阻挠议案还差几个席位，但他仍然愿意与他的新共和党同事合作。在与早间版的莱拉·法德尔的对话中，埃尔赛义德反思了最近的选举、民主党的未来以及未来几年制定有影响力的立法的必要性。

title_en: Cindy Holscher wins in Kansas, holding governor's office for Democrats
title_zh: 辛迪·霍尔舍 (Cindy Holscher) 在堪萨斯州获胜，代表民主党担任州长
summary: Holscher, a state senator, overcame a more well-known Republican who had Trump's endorsement in the state that has gone to the GOP in most other statewide races.
summary_zh: 霍尔舍尔是一名州参议员，他击败了一位更知名的共和党人，后者在该州得到了特朗普的支持，而在其他大多数州，该州都转向了共和党。
body_en: Cindy Holscher wins in Kansas, holding governor’s office for Democrats Holscher, a state senator, overcame a more well-known Republican who had Trump's endorsement in the state that has gone to the GOP in most other statewide races.

State Sen. Cindy Holscher has won the race for Kansas governor, keeping the office for Democrats in a state that leans Republican. Here she's seen speaking to reporters after casting her ballot during early voting at a polling location in Kansas City, Kansas. Jim Vondruska/Getty Images hide caption
Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher will hold onto the Kansas governor's office for her party after defeating Republican Ty Masterson, according to a race call by the Associated Press.

Masterson, the president of the state Senate, was endorsed by President Trump. Of the 36 elections for governor across the country, Kansas was seen as the most likely to flip from Democratic to Republican control.
The race call came after days of counting the provisional ballots and with local officials doing recounts in the closely contested election.

Current Democratic Gov. Laura Kelly is term-limited after serving for eight years in a state with a heavily Republican legislature and that usually votes for Republicans for other offices and in presidential elections.

Holscher, 57, ran a campaign with notes of populism, promising to fight "sweetheart deals" for billionaires. She tied Masterson to his work in the state Senate when it passed a tax cut under former Republican Gov. Sam Brownback that led to a series of budget crises and was later repealed.

Holscher opposed school vouchers, calling for more support for public schools, in contrast with Masterson, who backed school vouchers . She also called for a moratorium on new data centers and for legalizing cannabis as a way to generate state revenue.

Masterson, 57, called for lower property taxes and said faith influenced all his decisions, including in politics. He promised to be the "most pro-ag, pro-business, pro-oil and gas governor ," the state has seen. He called Holscher, "the most radical, liberal, socialist Democrat ever" on a ticket in Kansas.
"He likes to throw around a whole lot of labels," Holscher responded. "You know why? Because that's all he's got."

body_zh: 辛迪·霍尔舍尔（Cindy Holscher）在堪萨斯州获胜，为民主党人担任州长职位。霍尔舍尔是一名州参议员，她击败了一位更知名的共和党人，后者在该州得到了特朗普的支持，而在大多数其他全州竞选中，共和党人都支持了该州。
州参议员辛迪·霍尔舍尔 (Cindy Holscher) 赢得了堪萨斯州州长竞选，使民主党在这个倾向共和党的州保住了职位。照片中，她在堪萨斯州堪萨斯城的一个投票点提前投票后对记者发表了讲话。吉姆·冯德鲁斯卡/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
据美联社报道，民主党州参议员辛迪·霍尔舍尔(Cindy Holscher)在击败共和党人泰·马斯特森(Ty Masterson)后，将保住她所在政党的堪萨斯州州长职位。
州参议院议长马斯特森得到了特朗普总统的支持。在全国 36 次州长选举中，堪萨斯州被认为最有可能从民主党控制权转向共和党控制权。
经过几天的临时选票计票以及地方官员在这场竞争激烈的选举中重新计票后，选举结果发出了。
现任民主党州长劳拉·凯利(Laura Kelly)在一个共和党占多数立法机构的州任职八年后，任期受到限制，该州通常在其他职位和总统选举中投票支持共和党。
57 岁的霍尔舍尔发起了一场带有民粹主义色彩的竞选活动，承诺为亿万富翁争取“甜心交易”。她将马斯特森与他在州参议院的工作联系在一起，当时州参议院通过了前共和党州长萨姆·布朗巴克(Sam Brownback)领导下的减税政策，该减税政策导致了一系列预算危机，后来被废除。
霍尔舍尔反对学券，呼吁为公立学校提供更多支持，而马斯特森则支持学券。她还呼吁暂停新数据中心的建设，并使大麻合法化，以此作为增加国家收入的一种方式。
57 岁的马斯特森呼吁降低财产税，并表示信仰影响了他的所有决定，包括政治方面的决定。他承诺成为该州“最支持农业、支持商业、支持石油和天然气的州长”。他在堪萨斯州的一张选票上称霍尔舍尔为“有史以来最激进、最自由、最社会主义的民主党人”。
“他喜欢贴上很多标签，”霍尔舍尔回答道。 “你知道为什么吗？因为这就是他所拥有的一切。”

body_en: Donald Trump Jr exits as paid adviser for prediction market Kalshi | Donald Trump
Kalshi announces ‘mutual decision’ as Democrats say they plan to investigate Trump family’s investments
Donald Trump Jr is no longer a paid adviser for Kalshi, the prediction market company said Thursday.

Kalshi described it as a mutual business decision between the two parties that followed a decision by Trump Jr’s investment firm, 1789 Capital, to increase its investment in Kalshi’s biggest competitor Polymarket.
But the announcement comes a week after Democrats were able to take control of both the House and Senate in the midterm elections.
Democrats have said they planned to investigate the Trump family’s investments, including their business relationships with both prediction markets.

“We have mutually agreed to end Don’s advisory role after his firm’s significant investment in a competitor this past summer,” said Dani Lever, a spokesperson for Kalshi. “We are grateful for his contributions in helping us market Kalshi to more customers.”

The president’s eldest son became a paid “strategic adviser” for Kalshi shortly after President Trump was sworn into office for his second term in January 2025 and has been an investor in Polymarket since August 2025. Both companies have seen their popularity and use jump significantly in the past two years.

At the same time, both companies have received favorable treatment from the White House. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has backed the industry’s efforts to expand their products nationwide, including allowing their customers to trade sports-related contracts.
Both companies have adamantly denied that the financial relationship between Polymarket, Kalshi and the Trumps played any role in how the industry has been regulated under this administration.

1789 Capital increased its investment in Polymarket this past August, as part of Polymarket’s latest fundraising round. It was this investment that started the conversation about ending Trump Jr’s advisory role with Kalshi.
body_zh: 小唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump Jr) 辞去预测市场付费顾问的职务唐纳德·特朗普
卡尔希宣布“共同决定”，民主党人表示他们计划调查特朗普家族的投资
这家预测市场公司周四表示，小唐纳德·特朗普不再是卡尔希的付费顾问。
Kalshi 将其描述为双方共同的商业决定，此前小特朗普的投资公司 1789 Capital 决定增加对 Kalshi 最大竞争对手 Polymarket 的投资。
但这一消息是在民主党在中期选举中控制众议院和参议院一周后宣布的。
民主党人表示，他们计划调查特朗普家族的投资，包括他们与两个预测市场的业务关系。
Kalshi 发言人丹尼·利弗 (Dani Lever) 表示：“去年夏天，Don 的公司对竞争对手进行了重大投资，我们双方同意终止 Don 的顾问角色。” “我们感谢他为帮助我们向更多客户推销 Kalshi 所做的贡献。”
特朗普总统于 2025 年 1 月宣誓就职并开始第二个任期后不久，总统的长子就成为 Kalshi 的付费“战略顾问”，并自 2025 年 8 月以来一直是 Polymarket 的投资者。过去两年，这两家公司的受欢迎程度和使用率都大幅跃升。
同时，两家公司都得到了白宫的优惠待遇。商品期货交易委员会支持该行业在全国范围内拓展产品的努力，包括允许客户交易体育相关合约。
两家公司都坚决否认 Polymarket、Kalshi 和特朗普家族之间的财务关系在本届政府对该行业的监管中发挥了任何作用。
今年 8 月，1789 Capital 增加了对 Polymarket 的投资，作为 Polymarket 最新一轮融资的一部分。正是这项投资引发了关于结束小特朗普与卡尔希顾问角色的讨论。

title_en: Alaska judge rules a request by Peltola campaign for ballot data in Senate race is 'not reasonable'
title_zh: 阿拉斯加法官裁定佩尔托拉竞选团队要求提供参议院竞选选票数据的要求“不合理”
summary: An Alaska judge ruled Wednesday that a request by Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Mary Peltola's campaign for a list of absentee voters whose ballots have been rejected is "not reasonable," particularly given the time crunch election officials face as they co
summary_zh: 阿拉斯加法官周三裁定，美国参议院民主党候选人玛丽·佩尔托拉的竞选活动要求提供缺席选民名单
body_en: Becky Bohrer, Associated Press Becky Bohrer, Associated Press
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/alaska-judge-rules-a-request-by-peltola-campaign-for-ballot-data-in-senate-race-is-not-reasonable

JUNEAU, Alaska (AP) — An Alaska judge ruled Wednesday that a request by Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Mary Peltola's campaign for a list of absentee voters whose ballots have been rejected is "not reasonable," particularly given the time crunch election officials face as they continue counting ballots from last week's election.

Ballots are still being tallied in the ranked vote election, in which Peltola and two-term Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan are the main contenders. Alaska's is the only Senate race in the country that remained too early to call.

The state accepts ballots up to 15 days after general elections from overseas voters, making Nov. 18 the final day to receive them. That date is also the Division of Elections' target for conducting ranked vote tabulations if no candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes.

Attorneys for Peltola's campaign last Friday sued state elections officials, seeking a list of voters whose absentee ballots have been rejected and the reasons for the rejections. They said their intent was to ensure that all qualified voters have their ballots counted.

But attorneys for the state said the information requested would violate voter privacy. They also said producing such a list from a voter database would constitute an "electronic service or product" that under state law may not take priority over an agency's main responsibilities.

Superior Court Judge Thomas Matthews, in a written ruling, said that "in theory" records from the voter database could be redacted and produced in a way that would allow their release. But he said the division is not required to disclose the records requested by the campaign because they "cannot reasonably be produced at this juncture, nor redacted of confidential information."
The division has deadlines to meet and says its staff is working long hours to accomplish the agency's "fundamental responsibility" of administering elections, he wrote.
"The timing of the Campaign's request could simply not be worse," Matthews wrote.

An email seeking comment from one of the law firms representing Peltola's campaign was not immediately returned Wednesday, which was a holiday. The state Department of Law, which represented the Division of Elections, in a statement said it was pleased with Matthews' decision.

Abha Khanna, an attorney for Peltola's campaign, said during arguments Tuesday before Matthews the campaign wasn't seeking to disrupt the ballot counting process. She said the absentee ballot review process was going "incredibly smoothly."

But Khanna argued the information sought is a matter of public record and in line with what campaign observers have access to in locations where absentee review boards are meeting. The campaign wanted access to that information in a more centralized way, she said.

Attorneys for the state have argued that reports generated by the division with lists of ballots to be reviewed during the absentee ballot review process are not public records because they contain confidential information and are "ephemeral working documents that are not meant for preservation."

Michaela Thompson, who oversees the absentee ballot review boards for the division, said in an affidavit that the version of the report received by observers of the review process — including those affiliated with the campaigns — does not include as much confidential information but does include home addresses that many voters seek to keep private.
The observers sign confidentiality agreements and cannot keep, copy or record information in the report, she said.

The division's "old, inflexible" database cannot produce a report that excludes confidential addresses, meaning the agency would have to work with a vendor to create a more tailored report, Thompson said.
A free press is a cornerstone of a healthy democracy.
body_zh: 贝基·博勒 (Becky Bohrer)，美联社 贝基·博勒 (Becky Bohrer)，美联社
阿拉斯加州朱诺（美联社）——阿拉斯加州一名法官周三裁定，美国参议院民主党候选人玛丽·佩尔托拉的竞选活动要求提供选票被拒绝的缺席选民名单是“不合理的”，特别是考虑到选举官员在继续清点上周选举的选票时面临的时间紧迫。
排名投票选举仍在统计选票，佩尔托拉和两届共和党参议员丹·沙利文是主要竞争者。阿拉斯加是该国唯一一场还为时过早宣布的参议员竞选。
该州在大选后 15 天内接受海外选民的选票，因此 11 月 18 日是接收选票的最后一天。如果没有候选人赢得超过 50% 的首选票，该日期也是选举司进行排名选票统计的目标。
佩尔托拉竞选团队的律师上周五起诉了州选举官员，要求提供缺席选票被拒绝的选民名单以及拒绝的原因。他们表示，他们的目的是确保所有合格选民的选票都被清点。
但该州律师表示，所要求的信息将侵犯选民的隐私。他们还表示，从选民数据库中生成这样的名单将构成一种“电子服务或产品”，根据州法律，该服务或产品可能不会优先于机构的主要职责。
高等法院法官托马斯·马修斯在一份书面裁决中表示，“理论上”选民数据库中的记录可以被编辑并以允许发布的方式生成。但他表示，该部门不需要披露竞选活动所要求的记录，因为这些记录“目前无法合理地提供，也无法对机密信息进行编辑”。
他写道，该部门有最后期限，并表示其工作人员正在长时间工作，以完成该机构管理选举的“基本责任”。
马修斯写道：“竞选团队提出要求的时机再糟糕不过了。”
周三是假期，一封向代表佩尔托拉竞选活动的律师事务所寻求评论的电子邮件没有立即得到回复。代表选举部门的州法律部在一份声明中表示，对马修斯的决定感到满意。
佩尔托拉竞选团队的律师阿卜哈·卡纳 (Abha Khanna) 周二在马修斯面前的辩论中表示，竞选团队无意扰乱计票过程。她说缺席选票审查过程“非常顺利”。
但卡纳辩称，所寻求的信息是公共记录的问题，并且与竞选观察员在缺席审查委员会开会地点可以获得的信息一致。她说，竞选团队希望以更集中的方式获取这些信息。
该州律师辩称，该部门生成的包含缺席选票审查过程中要审查的选票清单的报告不是公共记录，因为它们包含机密信息，并且是“不适合保存的临时工作文件”。
监督该部门缺席选票审查委员会的米凯拉·汤普森(Michaela Thompson)在一份宣誓书中表示，审查过程观察员——包括与竞选活动有关的观察员——收到的报告版本没有包含那么多机密信息，但确实包含了许多选民寻求保密的家庭住址。
她说，观察员签署保密协议，不能保留、复制或记录报告中的信息。
汤普森说，该部门“旧的、不灵活的”数据库无法生成排除机密地址的报告，这意味着该机构必须与供应商合作来创建更具针对性的报告。
新闻自由是健康民主的基石。

title_en: Democrats want to stop Trump's arch, golf course and more. What are their options?
title_zh: 民主党人希望阻止特朗普的拱门、高尔夫球场等。他们的选择是什么？
summary: As Trump's arch and other projects make their way through the courts, many critics are looking to Congress to stop them. Democrats have a few tools, including funding and oversight.
summary_zh: 随着特朗普的拱门和其他项目进入法庭，许多批评者希望国会阻止它们。民主党有一些工具，我
body_en: Democrats vow to counter Trump's arch, golf course and more : NPR

Democrats vow to counter Trump's arch, golf course and more As Trump's arch and other projects make their way through the courts, many critics are looking to Congress to stop them. Democrats have a few tools, including funding and oversight.
President Trump signed the final steel beam at the White House ballroom the day after the midterm elections. Andrew Harnik/Getty Images hide caption
President Trump's efforts to remake Washington, D.C., have dominated his second term, even after his party's resounding midterm defeat.

He started his election week at the scandal-plagued Reflecting Pool and ended it with an order declaring his gilded Oval Office a national monument to "make it impossible for anybody ever to destroy this incredible space."
That proclamation, like any executive order, could be undone by a future president. But many of Trump's construction projects are changing D.C. in more permanent ways.
Trump aims to leave a physical legacy in D.C., bulldozing norms along the way

His administration has already downed hundreds of trees at East Potomac Park and demolished the East Wing of the White House to make space for a ballroom — which he called "the safest place in Washington" as he showed it to reporters the day after the midterms.

Trump has taken a uniquely unilateral approach to construction , packing regulatory commissions with his allies and bypassing Congress entirely. Most of his projects — from the triumphal arch to the Kennedy Center — are now playing out in court .
Critics accuse the Trump administration of skirting federal laws and misleading judges in its effort to progress as quickly as possible before the end of his term.
Judge orders an inquiry into potential DOJ misconduct in Trump's golf course case
Democrats have vowed to use their soon-to-be congressional majority to push back on what they describe as Trump's "vanity projects."

When asked about that, White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told NPR in an email that "no other president has done more to beautify our Nation's interior than President Trump." He cited park cleanups, the Reflecting Pool and the White House helipad and ballroom as examples, and said Democrats "should work with President Trump to make our nation's capital beautiful again."

Rep. Jared Huffman, center, poses with activists protesting Trump's triumphal arch at Memorial Circle in May. He will soon become the chair of the committee with legislative and oversight authority over public lands. Andrew Harnik/Getty Imags hide caption

Rep. Jared Huffman, D.-Calif., told NPR in an interview that the Trump administration has "played this game of Catch Me If You Can, where they roll ahead with the bulldozers and the tree cutters … and they wait for courts to shut them down." He says a Democrat-led Congress will fight back.

"There's no way that we could look away while these sacred, iconic places are being permanently changed in ways that violate the law and could have really terrible lasting impacts," said Huffman, the top Democrat on the House Natural Resources Committee, which has a legislative purview over public lands and national parks.
Kennedy relatives join the fight against Trump's arch, alleging harm to JFK's grave

Huffman says blocking Trump's construction projects — and holding people accountable for potential wrongdoing — will be a top priority when he leads the committee. Earlier this week, he sent letters ordering dozens of administration officials and private companies to preserve their records for a future investigation.
body_zh: 民主党人发誓要对抗特朗普的拱门、高尔夫球场等：NPR
民主党人发誓要对抗特朗普的拱门、高尔夫球场等 随着特朗普的拱门和其他项目进入法庭，许多批评者希望国会阻止它们。民主党有一些工具，包括资金和监督。
中期选举后的第二天，特朗普总统在白宫宴会厅签署了最后一根钢梁。安德鲁·哈尼克/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
特朗普总统重塑华盛顿特区的努力主导了他的第二个任期，尽管他的政党在中期选举中惨败。
他在丑闻缠身的倒影池开始了他的选举周，并以一项命令宣布他镀金的椭圆形办公室为国家纪念碑来结束选举周，“让任何人都无法破坏这个令人难以置信的空间”。
与任何行政命令一样，该公告可能会被未来的总统撤销。但特朗普的许多建设项目正在以更持久的方式改变华盛顿。
特朗普的目标是在华盛顿留下物质遗产，一路推倒规范
他的政府已经砍倒了东波托马克公园的数百棵树，并拆除了白宫东翼，为舞厅腾出空间——他在中期选举后的第二天向记者展示时称其为“华盛顿最安全的地方”。
特朗普采取了独特的单边建设方式，将监管委员会与他的盟友捆绑在一起，并完全绕过国会。他的大部分项目——从凯旋门到肯尼迪中心——现在都在法庭上进行。
批评者指责特朗普政府为了在任期结束前尽快取得进展而规避联邦法律并误导法官。
法官下令对司法部在特朗普高尔夫球场案中潜在的不当行为进行调查
民主党人发誓要利用即将成为国会的多数席位来反击他们所说的特朗普的“虚荣项目”。
当被问及此事时，白宫发言人戴维斯·英格尔在一封电子邮件中告诉美国国家公共广播电台，“没有其他总统比特朗普总统在美化我们国家内部方面做得更多。”他以公园清理、倒影池、白宫直升机停机坪和舞厅为例，并表示民主党人“应该与特朗普总统合作，让我们国家的首都再次美丽”。
五月，众议员贾里德·霍夫曼（中）与抗议特朗普在纪念圈的凯旋门的活动人士合影。他很快将成为该委员会的主席，拥有对公共土地的立法和监督权。安德鲁·哈尼克/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
加利福尼亚州众议员贾里德·霍夫曼 (Jared Huffman) 在接受 NPR 采访时表示，特朗普政府“玩了一场‘能者来抓我’的游戏，他们用推土机和砍树机向前推进……然后等待法院将其关闭。”他表示，民主党领导的国会将予以反击。
众议院自然资源委员会民主党领袖霍夫曼表示：“当这些神圣、标志性的地方正在以违反法律的方式永久改变，并可能产生真正可怕的持久影响时，我们绝不能视而不见。”该委员会对公共土地和国家公园拥有立法权限。
肯尼迪亲属加入反对特朗普拱门的斗争，声称肯尼迪坟墓遭到破坏
霍夫曼表示，阻止特朗普的建设项目并追究人们对潜在不当行为的责任将是他领导该委员会时的首要任务。本周早些时候，他致函命令数十名政府官员和私营公司保存他们的记录以供未来调查。

title_en: Senator opens investigation into evidence RFK Jr ‘unlawfully lied’ to Congress
title_zh: 参议员对小罗伯特·肯尼迪向国会“非法撒谎”的证据展开调查
summary: Exclusive: Ron Wyden, citing Guardian report, is launching inquiry into whether health secretary lied about Samoa trip during confirmation hearings A top Democratic senator has launched an investigation into evidence that Robert F Kennedy Jr “unlawfully lied”
summary_zh: 独家：罗恩·怀登（Ron Wyden）援引《卫报》的报道，正在调查卫生部长是否在确认听证会上对萨摩亚之行撒了谎
body_en: Exclusive: Ron Wyden, citing Guardian report, is launching inquiry into whether health secretary lied about Samoa trip during confirmation hearings

A top Democratic senator has launched an investigation into evidence that Robert F Kennedy Jr “unlawfully lied” in his 2025 confirmation hearings to become the US health secretary, citing a report by the Guardian .

Ron Wyden of Oregon, the incoming chair of the powerful Senate finance committee, is seeking extensive records from Children’s Health Defense (CHD), the non-profit anti-vaccine group Kennedy has used as a vehicle to fuel his political rise, including all documents related to a 2019 trip Kennedy took to Samoa.
RFK Jr lied in Senate confirmation hearings, newly revealed documents indicate

“We are beginning an investigation into evidence that Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F Kennedy, Jr unlawfully lied to Congress on multiple occasions,” Wyden said in a letter to the group that was sent on Wednesday and obtained by the Guardian. The letter was also signed by Angela Alsobrooks, a Democratic senator from Maryland.

In the letter, the two lawmakers cited reporting by the Guardian that indicated Kennedy lied about his reasons for going to Samoa in 2019, a trip that occurred just months before a measles outbreak killed 83 people in the Pacific island nation, mostly children under age five.

The trip, which Kennedy made as the chair and chief legal counsel of CHD, became one of the most criticized events in his career before he entered government. Critics, including Samoan officials, have said Kennedy’s presence emboldened anti-vaccine activists in Samoa, worsening a vaccination crisis. Kennedy has denied the allegations, saying he never gave any public statement about vaccines or discouraged Samoans from getting vaccinated.

“We are deeply concerned by the tactics Kennedy has used – both before and during his tenure as secretary – to stand in the way of children receiving life-saving vaccinations,” the two Democratic senators wrote. “In Samoa and in the United States, unvaccinated children have died tragic and preventable deaths during measles outbreaks. We intend to hold Secretary Kennedy accountable for the grave harm he has caused to vulnerable children. We also intend to hold him accountable for any false statements made to Congress, a crime that undermines the Senate’s ability to fulfill its constitutional duties.”
In two congressional confirmation hearings in January 2025, Kennedy told lawmakers who held the key to his confirmation that his visit to Samoa had “nothing to do with vaccines”.

But letters obtained by the Guardian and the Associated Press through an open records lawsuit brought by the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press contradicted that testimony. In one he wrote to the Samoan prime minister in January 2019 before the trip, Kennedy explicitly said he wanted to study the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine in the Pacific island nation. In it, he used the words “vaccine” or “vaccination” eight times.
The prime minister responded a month later , saying Samoa could benefit from CHD’s assessment of MMR vaccines and inviting him to come.
Children’s Health Defense did not respond to requests for comment, and the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) did not immediately comment.

HHS previously said in response to the Guardian’s reporting on Kennedy’s Senate testimony that his visit to Samoa was “unrelated to vaccines. Any claim or insinuation based on these letters that Secretary Kennedy lied under oath or to Congress is not only false but outright defamatory.” It has not provided a response to questions about why his testimony contradicted what he said in his letter to the Samoan prime minister.

By requesting documents from CHD, Wyden is aiming at the heart of Kennedy’s political machine. Since taking office, Kennedy has hired former CHD employees, including Lyn Redwood, a former CHD president who made early outreach on his behalf to Samoa . Redwood is now an employee at the HHS, reportedly working on vaccine safety . Kennedy’s closest adviser at HHS, Stefanie Spear, ran CHD’s newsletter before joining his 2024 presidential campaign.

With Kennedy now in government, CHD and its leaders often act as his most vociferous defenders, praising his work and explaining his decisions on their video podcasts, articles and on social media. Kennedy headlined CHD’s annual conference in September, where he made false and misleading claims about the safety of vaccines .

The Senate letter requested all documents related to any travel to Samoa by Kennedy or other employees or associates of CHD and any communications with Samoan government officials. It also asked for records related to Kennedy’s presidential campaign and his Senate confirmation process.
In addition, the senators requested records related to Kennedy’s speech to CHD’s September convention and all communications between CHD and federal government officials since 20 January 2025.

On the night of the election, after polls closed and it became clear Democrats would take a majority of seats in the Senate, Wyden made a social media post with a direct message about accountability. “ Subpoenas ,” he wrote, in the one-word post. Alsobrooks, a member of the Senate committee on health, education, labor and pensions, has repeatedly called on Kennedy to resign or be fired .

The letter does not go as far as the legal force of a subpoena. But it would be a good idea to treat such a letter seriously, said Tim Stretton , of the Project on Government Oversight, a nonpartisan watchdog group in Washington.
body_zh: 独家：罗恩·怀登（Ron Wyden）援引《卫报》的报道，正在调查卫生部长是否在确认听证会上对萨摩亚之行撒了谎
一位民主党高级参议员援引《卫报》的报道，对小罗伯特·肯尼迪 (Robert F Kennedy Jr) 在 2025 年美国卫生部长确认听证会上“非法撒谎”的证据展开了调查。
即将上任的参议院财政委员会主席、来自俄勒冈州的罗恩·怀登 (Ron Wyden) 正在向儿童健康保护组织 (CHD) 寻求大量记录，该组织是肯尼迪用来推动其政治崛起的非营利性反疫苗组织，其中包括与肯尼迪 2019 年萨摩亚之行相关的所有文件。
新披露的文件显示，小罗伯特·肯尼迪在参议院确认听证会上撒了谎
“我们正在开始调查卫生与公众服务部部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪多次非法向国会撒谎的证据，”怀登在周三发送给该组织的一封信中表示，该信由《卫报》获得。这封信还由马里兰州民主党参议员安吉拉·阿尔斯布鲁克斯 (Angela Alsobrooks) 签署。
两位议员在信中引用了《卫报》的报道，称肯尼迪在 2019 年前往萨摩亚的原因上撒了谎，这次旅行发生在麻疹爆发前几个月，这个太平洋岛国爆发了麻疹，导致 83 人死亡，其中大部分是五岁以下的儿童。
肯尼迪作为 CHD 主席兼首席法律顾问的这次访问成为他进入政府之前职业生涯中最受批评的事件之一。包括萨摩亚官员在内的批评者表示，肯尼迪的出现使萨摩亚的反疫苗活动人士更加大胆，从而加剧了疫苗接种危机。肯尼迪否认了这些指控，称他从未发表过任何有关疫苗的公开声明或劝阻萨摩亚人接种疫苗。
两位民主党参议员写道：“我们对肯尼迪在担任国务卿之前和担任国务卿期间所使用的阻碍儿童接种挽救生命的疫苗的策略深感担忧。” “在萨摩亚和美国，未接种疫苗的儿童在麻疹爆发期间惨遭死亡，但这些死亡是可以预防的。我们打算让肯尼迪国务卿对他对弱势儿童造成的严重伤害负责。我们还打算让他对向国会作出的任何虚假陈述负责，这种罪行损害了参议院履行宪法职责的能力。”
在2025年1月的两次国会确认听证会上，肯尼迪告诉掌握他确认关键的议员，他对萨摩亚的访问“与疫苗无关”。
但《卫报》和美联社通过新闻自由记者委员会提起的公开记录诉讼获得的信件与这一证词相矛盾。 2019 年 1 月，肯尼迪在出访前写给萨摩亚总理的一封信中明确表示，他希望在这个太平洋岛国研究麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹 (MMR) 疫苗。在其中，他八次使用了“疫苗”或“疫苗接种”等词。
一个月后，总理作出回应，称萨摩亚可以从 CHD 对 MMR 疫苗的评估中受益，并邀请他前来。
儿童健康保护组织没有回应置评请求，卫生与公共服务部 (HHS) 也没有立即置评。
美国卫生与公众服务部此前在回应《卫报》有关肯尼迪参议院证词的报道时表示，肯尼迪对萨摩亚的访问“与疫苗无关。任何基于这些信函声称肯尼迪国务卿在宣誓时或向国会撒谎的说法或影射不仅是虚假的，而且是彻头彻尾的诽谤。”对于为什么他的证词与他在给萨摩亚总理的信中所说的内容相矛盾的问题，它没有做出回应。

通过向 CHD 索取文件，怀登的目标是肯尼迪政治机器的核心。自上任以来，肯尼迪聘请了前 CHD 员工，其中包括前 CHD 总裁林恩·雷德伍德 (Lyn Redwood)，他很早就代表肯尼迪与萨摩亚进行了接触。雷德伍德现在是美国卫生与公众服务部的一名雇员，据报道从事疫苗安全工作。肯尼迪在 HHS 中最亲密的顾问斯蒂芬妮·斯皮尔 (Stefanie Spear) 在参加 2024 年总统竞选之前曾负责 CHD 的时事通讯。
随着肯尼迪入主政府，CHD 及其领导人经常充当他最有力的捍卫者，在视频播客、文章和社交媒体上赞扬他的工作并解释他的决定。肯尼迪在 9 月份的 CHD 年度会议上担任主角，他在会上对疫苗的安全性提出了虚假和误导性的主张。
参议院的信函要求提供与肯尼迪或 CHD 其他雇员或同事前往萨摩亚的任何旅行以及与萨摩亚政府官员的任何通信有关的所有文件。它还要求提供与肯尼迪总统竞选及其参议院确认程序相关的记录。
此外，参议员们还要求提供与肯尼迪在 CHD 9 月大会上的演讲相关的记录，以及自 2025 年 1 月 20 日以来 CHD 与联邦政府官员之间的所有通信记录。
选举当晚，民意调查结束后，民主党显然将在参议院占据多数席位，怀登在社交媒体上发帖，直接传达了有关问责的信息。 “传票，”他在一篇只有一个字的帖子中写道。参议院健康、教育、劳工和养老金委员会成员艾索布鲁克斯曾多次呼吁肯尼迪辞职或被解雇。
这封信没有达到传票的法律效力。但华盛顿无党派监督组织政府监督项目的蒂姆·斯特雷顿表示，认真对待这样一封信是个好主意。

title_en: White House warns of "blatant criminality" in Democratic probes
title_zh: 白宫警告民主党调查中存在“公然犯罪行为”
summary: White House counsel Will Scharf warned that congressional subpoenas could lead to investigations from the executive branch.
summary_zh: 白宫法律顾问威尔·沙夫警告说，国会传票可能会导致行政部门进行调查。
body_en: Top White House lawyer warns of "blatant criminality" in Democrats' investigations push - CBS News

Washington — The top lawyer in the White House warned the leading Democrat on the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee that investigations into the Trump administration that lawmakers plan to pursue in the next Congress "may cross the line into blatant criminality" and said congressional subpoenas could prompt probes from the executive branch.

The message from White House counsel Will Scharf to Rep. Robert Garcia, a California Democrat who is set to chair the Oversight Committee as of January, foreshadows a brewing fight between the Trump administration and congressional Democrats, who are poised to launch investigations in a slew of issues arising over the first two years of President Trump's second term.
Scharf sent a letter to Garcia, dated Monday, reminding him that investigative acts by Congress must be backed by a "legitimate legislative purpose."

"Beyond being inconsistent with the clear, well-recognized constitutional limitations on your investigative functions, threats to executive branch officials designed to deter them from public service, or process designed merely to abuse or instill fear in the recipient may cross the line into blatant criminality," Scharf wrote. "And issuing unlawful subpoenas with the intention of depriving citizens of their constitutional rights and privileges may warrant further investigation."

Scharf cited recent statements from Democratic members of Congress who previewed investigations into the Trump administration they plan to pursue once they take control of the House and Senate. He claimed that Democrats are intent on crossing the Constitution's limits on congressional investigations and subpoenas.

"Abusive threats and public statements about the indiscriminate issuance of subpoenas, along with threats directed at prospective targets within the Administration make it abundantly clear that any forthcoming investigative processes will be deployed to harass and aggrandize rather than to advance any legitimate end," he wrote.
Scharf accused Democrats of making "abusive and capricious threats" and said they are seeking to "abuse the legislative process to intimidate and to interfere with lawful functioning of government."
Garcia said in response to Scharf that the White House is threatening to infringe on his committee's right to conduct oversight.

"It appears Donald Trump has something to hide," the California Democrat said in a statement. "Let's be clear: Congress' authority comes from Article I of the Constitution, not from the permission of the White House. Congress has wide latitude to conduct investigations and oversight, an authority inherent in the power to legislate."
Garcia accused the Trump administration of weaponizing the executive branch against Congress.
"We are a co-equal branch of government and will not be deterred by baseless threats from a weaponized DOJ or from the President's lawyers," he said.

House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is poised to become speaker in January, told reporters that in the first two years of Mr. Trump's second term, the White House has been used to a GOP-led Congress that he said has been a "reckless rubber stamp" for the president's agenda.

"A Democratic Congress is going to be a check and balance on an out-of-control executive branch in the face of unprecedented corruption that they've unleashed on the American people, and if they don't like it, consult the Constitution," he said.
Molly Nixon, a senior fellow in executive power at the Cato Institute, said Scharf's warnings may be more political than legal in nature.

"This letter, I think, is sort of an opening salvo in what will ultimately be a political debate or a public argument about whether Congress is using its power legitimately, and I don't think that's likely to wind up in court, especially on a criminal charge, but is something Americans will be able to judge with their own eyes," she told CBS News.

While the executive branch could attempt to bring a criminal indictment, any prosecution would run into roadblocks because of the Constitution's Speech or Debate Clause, which immunizes lawmakers from criminal or civil actions stemming from legislative duties.
"I think it's incredibly unlikely that any court would find merit in any criminal charge against a member of Congress for their vote on issuing a subpoena," Nixon said.

Separate from Scharf's warning to House Democrats, Aaron Reitz, the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Texas, accused Connecticut Sen. Richard Blumenthal of threatening people who associated with Mr. Trump, after Blumenthal announced his plans to launch a congressional investigation into the companies and individuals who donated to the White House ballroom project.

In his Nov. 11 letter posted on X , Reitz appeared to accuse the senator of possibly committing a crime, citing two civil rights statutes that make it a crime to conspire to deprive people of their rights or to deprive someone of their rights "under the color of law."
body_zh: 白宫高级律师警告民主党推动的调查存在“公然犯罪行为” - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
华盛顿——白宫首席律师警告众议院监督和政府改革委员会的民主党领袖，议员们计划在下届国会对特朗普政府进行的调查“可能会跨越界限，成为公然的犯罪行为”，并表示国会传票可能会促使行政部门展开调查。
白宫顾问威尔·沙夫 (Will Scharf) 向加州民主党众议员罗伯特·加西亚 (Robert Garcia) 发出的信息预示着特朗普政府和国会民主党人之间即将爆发的斗争，后者准备对特朗普第二任期头两年出现的一系列问题展开调查。
沙夫于周一致函加西亚，提醒他国会的调查行动必须得到“合法立法目的”的支持。
沙夫写道：“除了违反宪法对调查职能的明确、公认的限制之外，对行政部门官员的威胁旨在阻止他们从事公共服务，或者旨在滥用或向接受者灌输恐惧的程序可能会越过界限，构成公然的犯罪行为。” “出于剥夺公民宪法权利和特权而发出非法传票的行为可能需要进一步调查。”
沙夫引用了国会民主党议员最近的声明，他们预览了一旦特朗普政府控制众议院和参议院，他们计划对特朗普政府进行的调查。他声称民主党人有意超越宪法对国会调查和传票的限制。
他写道：“滥用威胁和关于不分青红皂白发出传票的公开声明，以及针对政府内部潜在目标的威胁，非常清楚地表明，任何即将进行的调查程序都将用于骚扰和强化，而不是推进任何合法目的。”
沙夫指责民主党人发出“滥用和反复无常的威胁”，并表示他们正在寻求“滥用立法程序来恐吓和干扰政府的合法运作”。
加西亚在回应沙夫时表示，白宫威胁要侵犯他的委员会的监督权。
这位加州民主党人在一份声明中表示：“唐纳德·特朗普似乎有什么事情要隐瞒。” “让我们明确一点：国会的权力来自宪法第一条，而不是来自白宫的许可。国会拥有广泛的调查和监督自由度，这是立法权固有的权力。”
加西亚指责特朗普政府将行政部门武器化以对抗国会。
他说：“我们是平等的政府部门，不会被武器化的司法部或总统律师的毫无根据的威胁吓倒。”
众议院民主党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯(Hakeem Jeffries)即将在一月份成为众议院议长，他告诉记者，在特朗普第二任期的头两年，白宫已经习惯了共和党领导的国会，他称国会对总统的议程来说是“鲁莽的橡皮图章”。
他说：“面对美国人民遭受的前所未有的腐败，民主党国会将成为失控的行政部门的制衡者，如果他们不喜欢，请查阅宪法。”
卡托研究所行政权力高级研究员莫莉·尼克松表示，沙夫的警告本质上可能更具政治性，而不是法律性。
她告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻：“我认为，这封信是一场关于国会是否合法使用其权力的政治辩论或公开辩论的开场白，我认为这不太可能在法庭上结束，特别是在刑事指控上，但美国人将能够用自己的眼睛来判断。”
虽然行政部门可以尝试提起刑事起诉，但由于宪法的演讲或辩论条款，任何起诉都会遇到障碍，该条款使立法者免受因立法职责而产生的刑事或民事诉讼。
尼克松说：“我认为，任何法院都不太可能认为对国会议员因投票发出传票而提出的任何刑事指控有道理。”
除了沙夫向众议院民主党人发出警告之外，德克萨斯州南区联邦检察官亚伦·雷茨还指责康涅狄格州参议员理查德·布卢门撒尔威胁与特朗普有联系的人，此前布卢门撒尔宣布计划对向白宫宴会厅项目捐款的公司和个人展开国会调查。
雷茨在 11 月 11 日发布在 X 上的信中似乎指责这位参议员可能犯罪，并援引了两项民权法规，这些法规将密谋剥夺人们的权利或“以法律的名义”剥夺某人的权利定为犯罪行为。

title_en: Washington DC shooting: police identify victim and suspect – as it happened
title_zh: 华盛顿特区枪击事件：警方确认受害者和嫌疑人身份
summary: This blog is now closed. You can read our full report here: Police identify suspect and victim in Washington DC shooting The incident is shifting from an active shooter response to a barricaded subject response , a federal law enforcement official has told NBC
summary_zh: 该博客现已关闭。您可以在这里阅读我们的完整报告：警方确认了华盛顿特区枪击事件的嫌疑人和受害者。
body_en: It is nearly 6pm ET in Washington DC where a shooting this morning left 4 people injured and one person dead. Here is a wrap-up of the day’s key events and details

Police have identified the deceased victim as 46-year old James Stuart of northwest Washington DC . Police have also identified the suspect as 55-year old Matt Wade Lambert of northwest Washington DC, who died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.
2 men and 2 women were injured in the shooting. One of the victims is in critical condition while the others have non-life-threatening injuries.

Police said that the victim killed inside of the gym was the building manager for that location. They added that they believe the shooting was related to the suspect’s grievances with the building’s management over maintenance issues.

The suspect broke the gas line inside his apartment fireplace, police said, adding: “We know he started a fire.” “There were fire flames that were visible on the outside of the apartment building. We also know that there was gasoline and potential other flammable materials that were inside of his apartment,” police said.
Three firearms were located inside the suspect’s apartment. Those were a shotgun, a rifle and a handgun – all of which were used by the suspect.

VIDA Fitness, the gym at which the shooting unfolded, remains closed until further notice and access to the facility remains restricted. “We are devastated by the tragic loss of life at our Logan Circle location earlier today,” the gym owners said.

The justice department has set up a website for victims impacted by the shooting. The website includes resources for victim service providers, law enforcement, first responders, and community and faith leaders responding to the shooting.
body_zh: 美国东部时间下午 6 点左右，华盛顿特区今天早上发生枪击事件，造成 4 人受伤、1 人死亡。以下是当天的主要事件和详细信息的总结
警方已确认死者为华盛顿特区西北部的 46 岁詹姆斯·斯图尔特 (James Stuart)。警方还确认嫌疑人是华盛顿特区西北部的 55 岁马特·韦德·兰伯特 (Matt Wade Lambert)，他死于自伤枪伤。
枪击事件造成 2 名男子和 2 名女子受伤。其中一名受害者情况危急，其他人则没有生命危险。
警方表示，在健身房内被杀的受害者是该地点的大楼经理。他们补充说，他们认为枪击事件与嫌疑人对大楼管理人员在维护问题上的不满有关。
警方称，嫌疑人打破了公寓壁炉内的煤气管道，并补充说：“我们知道他引发了火灾。”警方表示：“公寓楼外部可见火焰。我们还知道他的公寓内有汽油和其他潜在的易燃材料。”
在嫌疑人的公寓内发现了三支枪支。这些是猎枪、步枪和手枪——所有这些都是嫌疑人使用的。
发生枪击事件的健身房 VIDA Fitness 仍处于关闭状态，直至另行通知，并且进入该设施仍受到限制。健身房老板表示：“今天早些时候，我们对洛根圆环店发生的悲惨生命损失感到震惊。”
司法部为受枪击事件影响的受害者建立了一个网站。该网站包括为受害者服务提供者、执法部门、急救人员以及应对枪击事件的社区和信仰领袖提供的资源。

title_en: Meet the 27-year old behind the protein ad that helped flip Mississippi
title_zh: 认识一下帮助扭转密西西比州的蛋白质广告背后的 27 岁人物
summary: One of this cycle’s biggest viral hits offers Democrats a potential blueprint as they think about competing in the South — and their digital strategy ahead of 2028.
summary_zh: 本周期最大的病毒式传播之一为民主党人思考在南方的竞争及其数字战略提供了潜在的蓝图
body_en: You know you’ve made a good ad when it’s outperforming an endorsement video from Barack Obama.

Ryan Sayles, a 27-year-old Mississippi content creator, is behind arguably the best political spot of the election cycle: Democrat Scott Colom’s viral “ pick another protein ” ad against GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.
You’ve probably seen it by now. The ad featured Mississippi voters’ blunt reactions to Hyde-Smith’s suggestion that people struggling with rising beef prices choose from other protein options.
“Pick another protein? Shiiii-, I’d rather pick another senator instead.”
“Pick another protein? She done lost her damn mind. I’d rather pick another senator.”
Sayles was at his nephew’s football game when he realized something extraordinary was happening.

“I was looking at the first numbers when it first dropped, and I was like, ‘Oh, this is about to be a really good video,’” he told POLITICO after Colom’s historic Senate race victory in the longtime Republican stronghold. “We had the Obama endorsement the day before, so that was our biggest video. It was like, ‘Dang, we ain’t ever gonna top that.’”
“And then this ad came, and we posted it, and it outperformed anything we ever did,” Sayles said.

The 30-second spot quickly became the talk of Mississippi and Washington, helping fuel Colom’s longshot campaign to unseat Hyde-Smith and become the first Black senator from the state since Reconstruction. And, it’s given Democrats across the country another blueprint for how to break through online ahead of a critical 2028 presidential race, as the party continues to rethink its strategy.

With the ad — and Colom’s win — Sayles has gone from a newcomer who stumbled into campaigning almost by accident to a name to watch in Democratic digital politics, as the party looks for fresh ways to reach voters ahead of 2028.

“[Sayles] should be considered the breakout-star of this cycle,” Colom wrote in a post on X about the viral ad earlier this month. “He’s going to be a giant in the media consultant game. He did GAME CHANGING work with SO little.”

In an interview with POLITICO, Sayles described how his lack of prior political experience shaped his approach to creating the ad and why he thinks Democrats should listen more closely to the voters they’re trying to reach. He also discussed the unexpected attention he’s received since the ad — and why he hopes Colom’s victory will serve as a wake-up call for the party to invest in the South.
This interview has been edited for length and clarity.
How did you get involved with the Colom campaign?

I did a lot of freelance videography and photography, and they really just needed a photographer for one event they were doing back in October. And I came and did video and pictures for him, and they kept me around.
They were like, "Yeah, we need to work with him,” and then from then on, I never left.
Take me behind the scenes of creating the protein ad. How did it come together?
Scott and his brother, Andrew, along with [the] campaign manager Gerard, they all plotted the script together, and so they presented it to me.
We filmed it, and I directed and made sure it [felt] like Mississippi. I guess I made it more Mississippi than what it was at the beginning.
You know, [I] just added the entertainment or funny pieces of it, like emphasizing the way he said the words and stuff like that. And then I shot it, edited it, and added the music to it.
body_zh: 当你的广告效果优于巴拉克·奥巴马的代言视频时，你就知道你制作了一个好广告。
瑞安·赛尔斯 (Ryan Sayles) 是一位 27 岁的密西西比州内容创作者，他可以说是选举周期中最好的政治热点的幕后黑手：民主党人斯科特·科洛姆 (Scott Colom) 针对共和党参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯 (Cindy Hyde-Smith) 制作的病毒式“选择另一种蛋白质”广告。
您现在可能已经看到了。该广告展示了密西西比州选民对海德·史密斯建议人们在牛肉价格上涨中应选择其他蛋白质选择的建议的直率反应。
“选择另一种蛋白质？什——，我宁愿选择另一位参议员。”
“选择另一种蛋白质？她真的疯了。我宁愿选择另一位参议员。”
塞尔斯正在观看他侄子的橄榄球比赛，这时他意识到发生了一些不寻常的事情。
“当它第一次下降时，我正在看第一个数字，我想，‘哦，这将是一个非常好的视频，’”在科罗姆在共和党的长期据点取得历史性的参议院选举胜利后，他告诉《政治》杂志。 “前一天我们得到了奥巴马的支持，所以这是我们最大的视频。就像，‘天哪，我们永远不会超越它。’”
“然后这个广告来了，我们发布了它，它的效果超过了我们以前做过的任何广告，”塞尔斯说。
这段 30 秒的广告很快成为密西西比州和华盛顿州的热门话题，帮助推动科罗姆推翻海德·史密斯并成为重建以来该州第一位黑人参议员的竞选活动。而且，随着该党继续重新思考其战略，它为全国各地的民主党人提供了如何在关键的 2028 年总统竞选之前在网上取得突破的另一幅蓝图。
随着这则广告以及科罗姆的胜利，塞尔斯从一个几乎是偶然进入竞选活动的新人，成为民主党数字政治中值得关注的人物，因为该党正在寻找在 2028 年之前吸引选民的新方式。
“[Sayles] 应该被视为这个周期的突破之星，”本月早些时候，Colom 在 X 上关于病毒式广告的一篇帖子中写道。 “他将成为媒体顾问行业的巨人。他用很少的钱做了改变游戏规则的工作。”
在接受 POLITICO 采访时，塞尔斯描述了他之前缺乏政治经验如何影响了他制作广告的方式，以及为什么他认为民主党应该更仔细地倾听他们试图接触的选民的声音。他还讨论了自广告发布以来他受到的意想不到的关注，以及为什么他希望科罗姆的胜利将成为该党投资南方的警钟。
为了篇幅和清晰度，本次采访经过编辑。
您是如何参与 Colom 活动的？
我做了很多自由摄像和摄影，他们实际上只需要一名摄影师来拍摄他们十月份所做的一次活动。我来为他制作视频和图片，他们让我留在身边。
他们说，“是的，我们需要和他一起工作，”从那时起，我就再也没有离开过。
带我走进制作蛋白质广告的幕后。它是怎么走到一起的？
斯科特和他的兄弟安德鲁，以及竞选经理杰拉德，他们一起策划了剧本，所以他们把它交给了我。
我们拍摄了它，我执导并确保它[感觉]像密西西比州。我想我让它比一开始更像密西西比州了。
你知道，[我]只是添加了其中的娱乐或有趣的部分，比如强调他说话的方式之类的。然后我拍摄它，编辑它，并添加音乐。

title_en: Rep. Bennie Thompson discusses the U.S. Senate race Democrat win in Mississippi
title_zh: 众议员本尼·汤普森讨论民主党在密西西比州的美国参议院竞选获胜
summary: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Democratic Representative Bennie Thompson, of Mississippi, about Democrat Scott Colom's U.S. Senate victory.
summary_zh: 美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 的米歇尔·马丁 (Michel Martin) 与密西西比州民主党众议员本尼·汤普森 (Bennie Thompson) 谈论民主党人斯科特·科罗姆 (Scott Colom) 在美国参议院的胜利。
body_en: Rep. Bennie Thompson discusses the U.S. Senate race Democrat win in Mississippi NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Democratic Representative Bennie Thompson, of Mississippi, about Democrat Scott Colom's U.S. Senate victory.
NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Democratic Representative Bennie Thompson, of Mississippi, about Democrat Scott Colom's U.S. Senate victory.
For more, I'm joined by Mississippi Congressman Bennie Thompson. He's represented the state's second district for more than 30 years. Good morning, Congressman. Thanks so much for joining us.

MARTIN: Good. Well, better now that I'm speaking to you. You came of age during the Civil Rights Movement, during the fight for voting rights in Mississippi. Now, be honest, what went through your mind when Scott Colom announced his run for the Senate? Did you think he could do it?

THOMPSON: Well, you know, I've been one of those people here in Mississippi who just felt that not only as a son of the South, Black people, in general, deserve better. My daddy, for instance, never was allowed to register and vote. And his son now serves as the highest-ranking elected official in the state until Scott Colom was elected senator here in the state. So I'm excited about that. I'm excited that it is happening, and you never give up. But to be honest with you, we knew that it would be a real tough slog to win, but Scott wanted to do it for all the right reasons. And so the rest is history.

MARTIN: It is history just made. So let's talk politics and then let's talk policy. First, the politics of it. Does this signal then that Democrats can be competitive across the country? 'Cause I do understand, and I think you have expressed some frustration that you think Democrats have not nationally, at least sort of the national political structure, been willing to invest in states in places that they have not considered winnable in recent years. Do you think that this signals a time that Democrats are now competitive nationwide and can be competitive nationwide?

THOMPSON: Well, I think Scott Colom's campaign proves that with proper investment, you can win. Our national infrastructure has yet to get that for candidates of color. Now I want to be clear. There are other candidates in the race this term for Senate and what have you, that had millions of dollars in their campaign coffers. Scott Colom was not one of them. What we had - candidates who were committed to making a difference in this state, come hell or high water - they put together whatever kind of event that was required. We put fish fries. We put spaghetti dinners. We had fundraisers in individuals' home. We had fundraisers at tailgates at football games, you name it. We did it. But we had a lot of volunteers. So we substituted what other campaigns - when they had money, we had people.

MARTIN: So before I let you go, as to policy, what do you want to see Senator-elect Colom emphasize going forward? I guess what I'm asking is, like, what do you think the top priorities should be for him as he undertakes this position?

THOMPSON: Well, let me tell you, it's very easy. We - a majority of our counties are medically underserved, so we need a senator who absolutely supports healthcare, whether it's for children, for seniors, access to healthcare is a key. We have educational systems that are woefully underfunded. So we need an education senator. We need someone who can help create economic development opportunities so that our children, when they get ready for the world of work, they'll have choices.

We are still exporting our most talented individuals to the benefit of other states because there's nothing here to do. For every dollar that we send to Washington, we get almost $3 back. So we're a needy state. We can't afford to have a senator that votes to cut Medicare, Medicaid, won't support Head Start, won't support the SNAP program, free and reduced meals for children, senior citizens programs. We just need a senator that votes to interests of a state like Mississippi. And in Scott Colom, we have that individual.
MARTIN: That is Congressman Bennie Thompson of Mississippi. Congressman, thank you so much for speaking with us.

body_zh: 众议员本尼·汤普森 (Bennie Thompson) 讨论民主党在密西西比州的参议院选举中获胜 NPR 的米歇尔·马丁 (Michel Martin) 与密西西比州的民主党众议员本尼·汤普森 (Bennie Thompson) 就民主党人斯科特·科洛姆 (Scott Colom) 在美国参议院的胜利进行了交谈。
美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 的米歇尔·马丁 (Michel Martin) 与密西西比州民主党众议员本尼·汤普森 (Bennie Thompson) 谈论民主党人斯科特·科罗姆 (Scott Colom) 在美国参议院的胜利。
如需了解更多信息，请听密西西比州国会议员本尼·汤普森 (Bennie Thompson) 的报道。他代表该州第二选区 30 多年。早上好，国会议员。非常感谢您加入我们。
马丁： 很好。好吧，现在更好了，我正在和你说话。你是在民权运动期间、在密西西比州争取投票权的斗争中长大的。现在，说实话，当斯科特·科罗姆宣布竞选参议员时，您的想法是什么？你认为他能做到吗？
汤普森：嗯，你知道，我是密西西比州的那些人之一，他们认为，不仅作为南方的儿子，黑人总体上应该得到更好的待遇。例如，我的父亲从未被允许登记和投票。他的儿子现在担任该州最高级别的民选官员，直到斯科特·科罗姆当选该州参议员。所以我对此感到很兴奋。我很高兴这一切正在发生，而且你永远不会放弃。但说实话，我们知道要获胜将是一场真正艰难的艰苦跋涉，但斯科特出于所有正确的理由想要这样做。所以剩下的就是历史了。
马丁：这是刚刚创造的历史。所以让我们先谈谈政治，然后再谈谈政策。首先，它的政治意义。那么这是否表明民主党可以在全国范围内具有竞争力？因为我确实理解，而且我认为你表达了一些沮丧，你认为民主党在全国范围内，至少在国家政治结构上，不愿意在他们认为近年来无法获胜的地方投资。您认为这是否标志着民主党现在在全国范围内具有竞争力并且可以在全国范围内具有竞争力的时代到来？

汤普森：嗯，我认为斯科特·科罗姆的竞选活动证明，只要投资得当，你就能获胜。我们的国家基础设施尚未为有色人种候选人提供这一服务。现在我想澄清一下。本学期还有其他候选人参加参议员竞选，你们的竞选金库里有数百万美元。斯科特·科罗姆不是其中之一。我们所拥有的——无论是地狱还是高水位，致力于在这个州做出改变的候选人——他们组织了所需的任何类型的活动。我们放了炸鱼薯条。我们晚餐吃的是意大利面。我们在个人家里举办筹款活动。我们在足球比赛的车尾举办筹款活动，凡是你能想到的。我们做到了。但我们有很多志愿者。所以我们取代了其他竞选活动——当他们有钱时，我们就有人。
马丁：所以在我让你离开之前，关于政策，你希望当选参议员科罗姆强调什么？我想我想问的是，你认为他担任这个职位时最优先考虑的事情是什么？
汤普森：好吧，让我告诉你，这很简单。我们大多数县的医疗服务不足，因此我们需要一位绝对支持医疗保健的参议员，无论是对于儿童还是老年人，获得医疗保健是关键。我们的教育系统资金严重不足。所以我们需要一位教育参议员。我们需要有人能够帮助创造经济发展机会，以便我们的孩子在为工作世界做好准备时有选择。
我们仍在输出我们最有才华的人才，以造福其他州，因为这里无事可做。我们每向华盛顿汇一美元，我们就能收回近 3 美元。所以我们是一个有需要的国家。我们不能让一位投票削减医疗保险、医疗补助、不支持 Head Start、不支持 SNAP 计划、儿童免费和减餐、老年人计划的参议员。我们只需要一位投票支持密西西比州这样的州利益的参议员。在斯科特·科洛姆（Scott Colom）身上，我们就有这样的人。
马丁：那是密西西比州国会议员本尼·汤普森。议员先生，非常感谢您接受我们的采访。

title_en: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race
title_zh: 民主党人斯科特·科洛姆赢得密西西比州参议员竞选
summary: Scott Colom has won the U.S. Senate race in Mississippi. After a very close race, he's the first Black man to represent the state in the Senate in nearly 150 years.
summary_zh: 斯科特·科洛姆赢得了密西西比州的美国参议员竞选。经过一场非常势均力敌的竞选后，他成为近邻州第一位代表该州进入参议院的黑人。
body_en: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race Scott Colom has won the U.S. Senate race in Mississippi. After a very close race, he's the first Black man to represent the state in the Senate in nearly 150 years.
Scott Colom has won the U.S. Senate race in Mississippi. After a very close race, he's the first Black man to represent the state in the Senate in nearly 150 years.
Last night in Mississippi, the U.S. Senate race was finally called. And history was made.
The state is now sending the first Black senator to Congress in nearly 150 years.

MARTÍNEZ: Elise Catrion Gregg of Gulf States Newsroom and Mississippi Public Broadcasting was at Senator-elect Scott Colom's victory party in Jackson - joins us now. Elise, what did the senator-elect have to say?

ELISE CATRION GREGG, BYLINE: Good morning. Well, first and foremost, he said a lot of thank-yous to his wife, his two young daughters, his campaign team and the voters. Colom has been confident for months that he'd win. And he certainly took the time to recognize that, but he also acknowledged that he didn't do it on his own.
SCOTT COLOM: It's not something that I did, y'all. It's something that we did.
COLOM: All I did was have the courage to imagine a night like this.
COLOM: I had the courage to believe in Mississippi.

GREGG: It was a tight race, though. And Colom, who ran on healthcare access and affordability, won by just shy of 5,000 votes, becoming the first Democrat to win a Senate race in nearly four decades and the first African American since Reconstruction.
MARTÍNEZ: I'm going to guess that the energy was high last night.
GREGG: Oh, yeah. I was at that rally and his watch party a week ago on election night. And if energy was high on election night, it was through the roof yesterday.
UNIDENTIFIED CROWD: (Chanting) We want Scott. We want Scott. We want Scott.

GREGG: People I spoke with last night just seem proud. You know, there was a lot of joy, a lot of excitement and no small amount of relief. The rally was at Tougaloo College, a historically Black institution. So plenty of students were there, including Nukia Tullis (ph), who's also a Mississippi native.

NUKIA TULLIS: It's just a thrilling experience, personally. It just goes to show that anything is possible. You're never too small. And your dreams are never too big for you to accomplish, and to just keep going, because this is truly amazing.
GREGG: And everybody had signs and banners cheering Colom on.
MARTÍNEZ: What do you think this means - this win means about the Deep South? What do we learn?
body_zh: 民主党人斯科特·科罗姆 (Scott Colom) 赢得密西西比州参议员竞选 斯科特·科罗姆 (Scott Colom) 赢得了密西西比州的美国参议员竞选。经过一场势均力敌的竞选，他成为近 150 年来第一位代表该州进入参议院的黑人。
斯科特·科洛姆赢得了密西西比州的美国参议员竞选。经过一场势均力敌的竞选，他成为近 150 年来第一位代表该州进入参议院的黑人。
昨晚在密西西比州，美国参议员竞选终于揭晓。历史被创造了。
该州现在正向国会派遣近 150 年来第一位黑人参议员。
马丁内斯：海湾国家新闻室和密西西比州公共广播公司的埃莉斯·卡特里昂·格雷格参加了当选参议员斯科特·科洛姆在杰克逊举行的胜利派对，现在加入我们。伊莉斯，当选参议员有什么话要说？
埃莉斯·卡特里恩·格雷格连线：早上好。首先，他对他的妻子、他的两个年幼的女儿、他的竞选团队和选民表示了很多谢意。几个月来，科罗姆一直对自己会获胜充满信心。他当然花了时间认识到这一点，但他也承认这不是他自己做的。
SCOTT COLOM： 这不是我做的，你们大家。这是我们所做的事情。
COLOM：我所做的就是鼓起勇气想象这样一个夜晚。
COLOM：我有勇气相信密西西比州。
格雷格：不过，这是一场激烈的比赛。以医疗保健获取和负担能力为主题的科洛姆以接近 5,000 票的优势获胜，成为近四十年来第一位赢得参议院竞选的民主党人，也是重建以来第一位非洲裔美国人。
马丁内斯：我猜昨晚的能量很高。
格雷格：哦，是的。一周前的选举之夜，我参加了那场集会和他的观看派对。如果说选举之夜的能量很高，那么昨天的能量就达到了顶峰。
不明身份的人群：（高呼口号）我们想要斯科特。我们想要斯科特。我们想要斯科特。
格雷格：昨晚与我交谈的人看起来都很自豪。你知道，当时有很多快乐、很多兴奋，还有不少的解脱。集会在图加卢学院(Tougaloo College)举行，这是一所历史悠久的黑人院校。那里有很多学生，其中包括密西西比人努基亚·图利斯 (Nukia Tullis)（博士）。
NUKIA TULLIS：就我个人而言，这真是一次激动人心的经历。它只是表明一切皆有可能。你永远不会太小。你的梦想永远不会太大而让你无法实现，并继续前进，因为这确实令人惊奇。
格雷格：每个人都举着标语和横幅为科罗姆加油。
马丁内斯：您认为这意味着什么？这场胜利对南方腹地意味着什么？我们学到什么？

title_en: Major AI developers can't control their own tech, lawsuit alleges
title_zh: 诉讼称，主要人工智能开发商无法控制自己的技术
summary: Companies including Anthropic, Meta and OpenAI are knowingly building technology that poses catastrophic risks to humanity, nonprofit groups claim in a lawsuit.
summary_zh: 非营利组织声称，包括 Anthropic、Meta 和 OpenAI 在内的公司正在故意开发对人类构成灾难性风险的技术。
body_en: Anthropic, OpenAI and other AI developers can't control their own tech, new lawsuit alleges - CBS News

A coalition of nonprofit groups sued five major artificial intelligence developers on Thursday in a bid to block their development of AI models, alleging the companies knowingly created technology that poses catastrophic risks to humanity.

The lawsuit — filed in San Francisco Superior Court by the Alliance for Secure AI, alongside advocacy groups Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen and the Heat Initiative — named Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceXSI (SpaceX Super Intelligence).
"For years, the executives building these systems have warned us that their own frontier models pose catastrophic risks," Brendan Steinhauser, CEO of The Alliance for Secure AI, said in a statement.
"Yet they keep racing to develop and market increasingly powerful AI that they admit they cannot reliably control, and are now handing over AI research and development to AI itself," he added.
The tech companies targeted in the suit did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The litigation comes amid broader concerns about AI safety , sparked by several publicly reported incidents in which AI agents went rogue and carried out unauthorized actions.

The nonprofit groups contend that AI companies are developing technology they have admitted they can't control. The risk could grow as the companies rely more on their own AI models to develop future platforms without human intervention, a concept known as "recursive self-improvement," according to the suit.

"Defendants know these systems do not consistently act in accordance with their intentions," the lawsuit states. "And Defendants know there is no reliable method to control their AI systems and prevent them from causing harm."

The nonprofits also point to past comments by AI company executives acknowledging the potential harm from their technology. In 2015, for example, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said AI will "probably most likely lead to the end of the world." In 2025, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei suggested there was a 25% chance that the development of AI could lead to disastrous outcomes.

As scrutiny of their tech's safety grows, tech leaders have underlined their safety commitments. AI company leaders, including Altman, Amodei and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, in October voiced support for an industrywide slowdown in AI development after an Anthropic employee said there's a 10% chance AI "could kill all humans."

该诉讼由安全人工智能联盟 (Alliance for Secure AI) 以及不可替代教育基金 (Irreplaceable Education Fund)、公共公民 (Public Citizen) 和 Heat Initiative 等倡导组织向旧金山高等法院提起，名为 Anthropic、谷歌、Meta、OpenAI 和 SpaceXSI (SpaceX Super Intelligence)。
安全人工智能联盟首席执行官布伦丹·斯坦豪瑟在一份声明中表示：“多年来，构建这些系统的高管一直警告我们，他们自己的前沿模型会带来灾难性风险。”
他补充道：“然而，他们仍在竞相开发和销售日益强大的人工智能，但他们承认自己无法可靠地控制这些人工智能，并且现在将人工智能的研发工作交给了人工智能本身。”
该诉讼针对的科技公司没有立即回应置评请求。
此次诉讼正值人们对人工智能安全产生更广泛的担忧之际，几起公开报道的人工智能代理失控并进行未经授权的行动的事件引发了人们的担忧。
这些非营利组织声称，人工智能公司正在开发他们承认无法控制的技术。诉讼称，随着公司更多地依赖自己的人工智能模型来开发未来平台而无需人工干预，这种风险可能会增加，这一概念被称为“递归自我改进”。
诉讼称：“被告知道这些系统并不总是按照他们的意图行事。” “被告知道没有可靠的方法来控制他们的人工智能系统并防止它们造成伤害。”
这些非营利组织还提到了人工智能公司高管过去的言论，承认他们的技术存在潜在危害。例如，2015 年，OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 表示，人工智能“很可能会导致世界末日”。 Anthropic 首席执行官 Dario Amodei 表示，到 2025 年，人工智能的发展有 25% 的可能性会导致灾难性后果。
随着对其技术安全的审查不断加强，技术领导者强调了他们的安全承诺。 10 月份，Altman、Amodei 和 SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 等人工智能公司领导者在 Anthropic 员工表示人工智能“可能杀死所有人类”的可能性为 10% 后，表示支持全行业放缓人工智能开发速度。

title_zh: 数十名抗议者在查克·舒默的华盛顿办公室静坐后被捕
summary: Protesters with the Sunrise Movement youth climate group push for new Senate leadership and ending the filibuster Dozens of protesters with the Sunrise Movement, a youth climate organization, were arrested after staging a sit-in inside Senate minority leader C
summary_zh: 日出运动青年气候组织的抗议者推动新的参议院领导层并结束阻挠数十名日出运动的抗议者
body_en: Dozens of protesters arrested after staging sit-in at Chuck Schumer’s DC office | Chuck Schumer
Protesters with the Sunrise Movement youth climate group push for new Senate leadership and ending the filibuster
Dozens of protesters with the Sunrise Movement, a youth climate organization, were arrested after staging a sit-in inside Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer’s Washington DC office Thursday

According to the Sunrise Movement, 54 people were arrested, among a few hundred who joined the protest from across the country, including some from New York, which Schumer represents. On its Instagram, the group is fundraising $24,000 to cover the bail fees and any potential legal fees for those arrested.
Capitol police were not immediately available for comment.

In a clip on the Sunrise Movement’s Instagram , with over 40,000 likes at the time of publication, young people sitting on the office floor chanted: “Hey hey, ho ho, Schumer has got to go!” Protesters, including children, held signs reading “The filibuster kills,” “Stop the climate crisis,” and “Schumer: Step up or step aside.”

As Senate Democrats prepare to vote on a majority leader for the upcoming Congress, they’re wrestling with how to navigate what feels like a clear mandate for anti-establishment voices from communities historically underrepresented in federal office to step into leadership. Several Democratic senators have said they will not support Schumer for the position, including Bernie Sanders , an independent who caucuses with the Democrats, as well as several members of the freshman class , like Michigan’s Abdul El-Sayed and South Carolina’s Annie Andrews.
Some have backed Maryland’s Chris Van Hollen as a challenger, including Peggy Flanagan, Minnesota’s senator-elect, and 50501 , one of the major groups behind the No Kings protests.

The protesters on Thursday delivered a letter to Schumer arguing, per the group’s press release, that “after a collective decade of Schumer leadership it was time for change” and demanding Democrats prioritize ending the filibuster when Congress returns in January.

They also dropped the letters at the offices of every Senate Democrat. According to the Sunrise Movement’s campaigns director, Kidus Girma, Thursday’s action is one of several planned over the next two weeks targeting Senate Democrats and “demanding they actually take action”.

The group has regularly protested against politicians since first making headlines in 2018 with another sit-in targeting then-House speaker Nancy Pelosi , and helped launch calls for a Green New Deal alongside congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who was part of that 2018 sit-in. In the eight years since, Sunrise has supported progressive candidates, and last week, a Sunrise co-founder, Will Lawrence, 36, won his race for a Michigan US House seat after campaigning against datacenters.

“Young people went to Senator Chuck Schumer’s office to demand a Senate majority leader that would fight for the young people who elected a historic blue wave last week. They’re demanding change, not the same old, same old,” said Girma over the phone.

According to early data from Tufts University’s Center for Information and Research on Civic Learning and Engagement (Circle), which monitors youth civic engagement, the 3 November elections saw the second-highest youth turnout for a midterm election in 30 years – following only the 2018 midterms in Donald Trump’s first term.
“Chuck Schumer has been in office longer than I have been alive, and I’m 31 years old,” Girmus said. “[Young people] didn’t vote for a return to the Biden years, but rather a change.”

This isn’t the first sit-in of Schumer’s office organized by young people to happen this week. On Tuesday, three protesters were arrested during a protest by the youth advocacy group Get Free, who were there saying voters “need Democratic leaders to meet the moment lest we repeat history again”, according to executive director Nicole Carty.
Last week, Girma said the election outcome “shows that young people deeply, deeply care about their futures and the current government – but also, they’re making clear demands around how to fix it”.
body_zh: 数十名抗议者在查克·舒默的华盛顿办公室静坐后被捕 |查克·舒默
日出运动青年气候组织的抗议者推动新的参议院领导层并结束阻挠
周四，青年气候组织“日出运动”的数十名抗议者在参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默的华盛顿特区办公室内静坐后被捕
据“日出运动”称，全国各地参加抗议活动的数百人中有 54 人被捕，其中包括一些来自舒默代表的纽约的人。该组织正在其 Instagram 上筹款 24,000 美元，用于支付被捕者的保释费和任何潜在的法律费用。
国会警方未能立即发表评论。
在日出运动 Instagram 上的一段视频中，截至发布时已有超过 40,000 个赞，坐在办公室地板上的年轻人高呼：“嘿嘿，嗬嗬，舒默必须走！”包括儿童在内的抗议者举着标语，上面写着“阻挠致人死亡”、“阻止气候危机”和“舒默：站起来，否则就让位”。
当参议院民主党人准备投票选出即将到来的国会的多数党领袖时，他们正在努力思考如何明确授权来自联邦办公室历来代表性不足的社区的反建制声音进入领导层。几位民主党参议员表示，他们不会支持舒默担任这一职务，其中包括与民主党同组的独立党员伯尼·桑德斯，以及密歇根州的阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛义德和南卡罗来纳州的安妮·安德鲁斯等几名新生。
一些人支持马里兰州的克里斯·范·霍伦作为挑战者，其中包括明尼苏达州当选参议员佩吉·弗拉纳根和“无国王”抗议活动背后的主要团体之一“50501”。
根据该组织的新闻稿，抗议者周四向舒默递交了一封信，称“在舒默领导了十年之后，是时候进行变革了”，并要求民主党在国会一月份回归时优先结束阻挠议事活动。
他们还将这些信件扔到了每位参议院民主党人的办公室。日出运动的竞选总监基杜斯·吉尔马表示，周四的行动是未来两周计划针对参议院民主党人并“要求他们实际采取行动”的几项行动之一。
自 2018 年首次因针对时任众议院议长南希·佩洛西的静坐而成为头条新闻以来，该组织经常抗议政客，并与参加 2018 年静坐的国会女议员亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯一起帮助发起绿色新政呼吁。此后的八年里，Sunrise 一直支持进步候选人，上周，Sunrise 联合创始人、36 岁的威尔·劳伦斯 (Will Lawrence) 在反对数据中心的竞选活动后赢得了密歇根州美国众议院席位的竞选。
“年轻人来到参议员查克·舒默的办公室，要求一位参议院多数党领袖为上周选出历史性蓝色浪潮的年轻人而战。他们要求改变，而不是老样子，”吉尔马在电话中说。
根据监测青年公民参与的塔夫茨大学公民学习和参与信息与研究中心 (Circle) 的早期数据，11 月 3 日的选举出现了 30 年来第二高的中期选举青年投票率，仅次于唐纳德·特朗普第一任期的 2018 年中期选举。
“查克·舒默在任的时间比我在世的时间还要长，而我已经 31 岁了，”吉尔姆斯说。 “[年轻人]没有投票支持回到拜登时代，而是支持改变。”
这并不是本周首次由年轻人组织的舒默办公室静坐活动。周二，三名抗议者在青年倡导组织“自由”的抗议活动中被捕，据执行董事妮可·卡蒂称，他们在那里表示选民“需要民主党领导人立即会面，以免我们再次重演历史”。
吉尔马上周表示，选举结果“表明年轻人非常非常关心他们的未来和现任政府，而且他们也对如何解决这个问题提出了明确的要求”。

summary_zh: 纽约市长佐兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 表示，救援人员正在“极其危险的条件”下寻找被困人员 救援人员仍在继续搜寻
body_en: New York mayor Zohran Mamdani says crews are working in ‘extremely dangerous conditions’ to find anyone trapped
Rescue crews have continued to search for survivors in the rubble of a collapsed building in Brooklyn, New York , as the death toll rose to eight.

Six people were ​found dead in the wreckage and two ‌others died later from their injuries, according to city ‌officials. Two of those killed were children and another two have been identified as construction workers from a nearby site.

At least an additional 18 people were hurt when the three-storey residential building on the edge of a construction site in New York City’s Flatbush neighbourhood collapsed at about 4pm on Wednesday. Of the 18 injured, four were firefighters who led the rescue effort.

Zohran Mamdani , the mayor of New York City, said in a post on X on Thursday morning that he was “heartbroken” by the tragedy. He urged the public to stay away from the site on Flatbush Avenue, where about 250 first responders from the New York City fire department (FDNY) worked through what Mamdani said were “extremely dangerous conditions” to find anybody still trapped.
Speaking as torrential rain drenched the area, Mamdani said the weather would hinder but not stop the search.
“Conditions will get more challenging today with the rain, but operations will continue,” he said.
The New York fire commissioner, Lillian Bonsignore, said crews were still searching for survivors Thursday afternoon.
“We have not shifted from rescue to recovery,” Bonsignore said. “We are still in the search and rescue phase.”

“We always assume there are more people there until we can access the ground,” Bonsignore said. “So until we remove some of the bigger debris and are able to search beneath them, this will remain a rescue operation.”

Thursday afternoon, the FDNY said rescue workers had finished searching the collapse site as of 3.37pm local time after they determined there were no remaining victims. The site was then turned over to the New York police department (NYPD) and the city’s department of buildings.

Workers brought in an excavator in the early hours of Thursday to help move larger pieces of wreckage from the building, which had housed a number of apartments. Drones and canine units were being used to assist the rescue effort.

Video taken at the scene on Wednesday night showed crews removing several people on stretchers. One person, seen covered in dust, was extricated at about 6.30pm after a crew dug a hole through some of the debris.
Another person rescued was a woman who was six months pregnant, whose husband had been searching for her through the late afternoon, New York ABC News affiliate WABC reported .
“I have an update. She is alive, she is still alive. I am very happy,” the man told the outlet.

Dozens of onlookers, some in tears, gathered to watch the rescue operation. Lillian Bonsignore, the FDNY commissioner, told a crowd at an evening press conference: “We know that we are not finished here, and we will likely not be finished for quite some time.”

Adding to the urgency of the situation was a weather forecast that predicted heavy rain with a chance of thunderstorms and gusty winds moving through the borough from lunchtime and through Thursday afternoon.
Several people who were made homeless by the collapse took shelter in the Bethesda church of God in Christ opposite the site.
Kathy Hochul, the New York governor, called the collapse “absolutely heartbreaking” on Thursday morning at a press conference on a small business initiative in Harlem.
body_zh: 纽约市长佐兰·马姆达尼表示，工作人员正在“极其危险的条件下”寻找被困人员
救援人员继续在纽约布鲁克林一栋倒塌建筑的废墟中寻找幸存者，死亡人数上升至八人。
据市政府官员称，残骸中发现六人死亡，另外两人后来因伤重死亡。其中两名遇难者是儿童，另外两人已被确认为附近工地的建筑工人。
周三下午 4 点左右，纽约市弗拉特布什社区一处建筑工地边缘的一栋三层住宅楼倒塌，至少造成 18 人受伤。 18 名受伤人员中，有 4 名是领导救援工作的消防员。
纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 周四早上在 X 上发帖表示，他对这起悲剧感到“心碎”。他敦促公众远离弗拉特布什大道（Flatbush Avenue）的现场，纽约市消防局（FDNY）约 250 名急救人员在马姆达尼所说的“极其危险的条件”下寻找仍然被困的人。
马姆达尼表示，暴雨淹没了该地区，天气会阻碍但不会停止搜寻工作。
他说：“由于今天下雨，情况将变得更加困难，但运营仍将继续。”
纽约消防专员莉莲·邦西诺尔 (Lillian Bonsignore) 表示，周四下午，工作人员仍在寻找幸存者。
“我们还没有从救援转向恢复，”邦西诺尔说。 “我们仍处于搜救阶段。”
“我们总是假设那里有更多的人，直到我们能够到达地面，”邦西诺尔说。 “因此，在我们清除一些较大的碎片并能够在其下方进行搜索之前，这仍将是一项救援行动。”
周四下午，纽约消防局表示，救援人员在确定没有剩余遇难者后，截至当地时间下午 3 点 37 分已完成对倒塌现场的搜索。该网站随后被移交给纽约警察局 (NYPD) 和市建筑部门。
周四凌晨，工人们搬来了一台挖掘机，帮助从大楼内移出较大的残骸，该大楼内有许多公寓。无人机和警犬部队被用来协助救援工作。
周三晚上在现场拍摄的视频显示，工作人员用担架抬走了几人。下午 6 点 30 分左右，工作人员在一些碎片中挖了一个洞，一名浑身灰尘的人被救出。
据纽约广播公司新闻附属机构 WABC 报道，另一名获救者是一名怀孕六个月的妇女，她的丈夫整个下午都在寻找她。
“我有最新消息。她还活着，她还活着。我很高兴，”该男子告诉媒体。
数十名围观者聚集在一起观看救援行动，其中一些人热泪盈眶。纽约消防局局长莉莲·邦西诺雷 (Lillian Bonsignore) 在晚间新闻发布会上对人群表示：“我们知道我们的任务还没有结束，而且很可能在相当长的一段时间内都不会结束。”
天气预报预测，从午餐时间到周四下午，该行政区将出现大雨，并有可能出现雷暴和阵风，这让情况变得更加紧迫。
一些因倒塌而无家可归的人在现场对面的贝塞斯达基督教堂避难。
周四上午，纽约州州长凯西·霍赫尔 (Kathy Hochul) 在哈莱姆区一项小企业倡议新闻发布会上称，这次倒塌“绝对令人心碎”。
