summary_zh: 由于专家担心繁忙的水道带来的危险，该物种的目击事件变得越来越普遍。周四，人们发现了一头座头鲸。
body_en: Sightings of the species are becoming increasingly common as experts worry about danger posed by busy waterways
A humpback whale was spotted on Thursday swimming in New York’s Hudson River, sparking a social media frenzy.

Brad Hoylman-Sigal, president of Manhattan borough, was among those to share a photograph of the whale on Facebook , an image taken on Thursday morning and provided by Gotham Whale, a citizen science and education group that tracks marine mammals in New York’s waterways.
The group’s own post on X appealed for more information and photographs of the whale in an effort to help identify its origin and calculate its size.
On its Facebook page, it posted a short video of the whale rolling over and spraying water from its blowhole as a group of onlookers cheered. The whale was still present by early afternoon.
It is not known whether the whale is male or female, or if it arrived in the Hudson alone, or was swimming with company.
Humpback whales are usually solitary by nature, according to the environmental group Whale Trail , but can sometimes be spotted in groups upto 10 to 15 when feeding, or in short-term social groups.
Adult males can grow up to 48ft (14.6 meters) and weigh as much as 40 tons (36,287kg).

Sightings of humpbacks in the New York, once rare, are becoming increasingly common. In 2018, 272 whales were spotted in the city’s waters, Gotham Whale told the Guardian , and the group has documented numerous glimpses since.
As numbers have increased, however, so has the risk to the whales from shipping and other hazards.
The New York Times reported in January that more whales were found stranded, likening the danger to the species in New York’s busy waterways as “like deer crossing the road”.
body_zh: 由于专家担心繁忙水道带来的危险，该物种的目击事件变得越来越普遍
周四，人们发现一头座头鲸在纽约哈得逊河游泳，引发了社交媒体的热议。
曼哈顿区长布拉德·霍伊尔曼-西格尔 (Brad Hoylman-Sigal) 是在 Facebook 上分享鲸鱼照片的人之一，这张照片于周四早上拍摄，由 Gotham Whale 提供，Gotham Whale 是一个追踪纽约水道海洋哺乳动物的公民科学和教育组织。
该组织自己在 X 上发布的帖子呼吁提供更多关于鲸鱼的信息和照片，以帮助确定其起源并计算其大小。
在其 Facebook 页面上，该公司发布了一段短视频，视频中鲸鱼翻滚并从喷水孔喷水，一群围观者欢呼雀跃。到下午早些时候，鲸鱼仍然存在。
目前尚不清楚这头鲸鱼是雄性还是雌性，也不知道它是独自抵达哈德逊河，还是与同伴一起游泳。
根据环保组织 Whale Trail 的说法，座头鲸通常是独居的，但有时在进食时会发现多达 10 至 15 只的群体，或者是短期的社会群体。
成年雄性可长至 48 英尺（14.6 米），体重可达 40 吨（36,287 公斤）。
座头鲸在纽约的目击事件曾经很少见，但现在变得越来越常见。 Gotham Whale 告诉《卫报》，2018 年，在该市水域发现了 272 头鲸鱼，此后该组织记录了许多鲸鱼的踪迹。
然而，随着鲸鱼数量的增加，运输和其他危险对鲸鱼造成的风险也随之增加。
《纽约时报》一月份报道称，更多鲸鱼被发现搁浅，并将纽约繁忙水道中的鲸鱼面临的危险比作“就像鹿过马路一样”。

title_en: CDC reports six measles deaths in 2026 as US battles worst outbreak in 35 years
title_zh: 美国疾病预防控制中心 (CDC) 报告 2026 年将有 6 人因麻疹死亡，美国正在应对 35 年来最严重的麻疹疫情
summary: Figures highlight spread of virus, officially declared eliminated in US in 2000, but CDC does not identify which states accounted for deaths The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported six measles-related deaths in the US this year, according
summary_zh: 数据突显病毒的传播，2000 年美国正式宣布消灭该病毒，但 CDC 并未确定哪些州造成了死亡
body_en: Figures highlight spread of virus, officially declared eliminated in US in 2000, but CDC does not identify which states accounted for deaths

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported six measles-related deaths in the US this year, according to figures published on its website on Thursday, as the country faces its most severe resurgence of the disease in decades.
The newly reported total is twice the number of deaths recorded in 2025, highlighting the spread of the highly infectious virus, which was officially declared eliminated in the US in 2000.

The country is currently experiencing its largest measles outbreak since 1991. More than 5,400 cases reported nationwide, according to data from the Johns Hopkins University International Vaccine Access Center tracker .

Pennsylvania has been the state most severely affected by the outbreak, with officials confirming six measles-associated deaths in the state this year. A child also died in New York on election day, followed days later by the death of an infant in Wisconsin. Active outbreaks have been reported in nearly every US state.
The Wisconsin department of health services confirmed the infant’s death, while New York recorded its first known measles-related fatality in more than three decades.
The CDC did not identify which states accounted for the six deaths included in its official count.

The difference in the reported figures followed a change in how the CDC, operating under US health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, tracks measles fatalities . The CDC is now using data from the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS), which is a way to track mortality trends over time, according to a note published to the agency’s website on 4 September.

Kennedy previously argued without evidence that two of the deaths in Pennsylvania may not be from measles. He asked Erica Schwartz, the CDC’s director, not to count the deaths in the official CDC tally, according to reporting by Reuters. The day after the Reuters report was published, the CDC changed its data source on measles deaths.
Measles is preventable through the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine, which offers approximately 97% protection after two doses.

The US could lose its measles elimination status this week, a development likely to further define Kennedy ’s legacy of interference in vaccine policies. Losing that designation would place the US alongside Canada and several countries in Europe and Asia where measles had previously been eliminated before making a comeback.
body_zh: 数字强调了病毒的传播，该病毒于 2000 年在美国正式宣布被消灭，但 CDC 并未确定哪些州造成了死亡
美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 周四在其网站上公布的数据显示，今年美国有六例与麻疹相关的死亡，该国面临着数十年来最严重的麻疹疫情卷土重来。
新报告的死亡人数是 2025 年记录的死亡人数的两倍，突显了这种高传染性病毒的传播，该病毒于 2000 年在美国被正式宣布消灭。
该国目前正在经历自 1991 年以来最大规模的麻疹疫情。根据约翰·霍普金斯大学国际疫苗获取中心追踪数据，全国报告了 5,400 多例麻疹病例。
宾夕法尼亚州是受疫情影响最严重的州，官员确认该州今年有六例与麻疹相关的死亡。选举日当天纽约也有一名儿童死亡，几天后威斯康星州也有一名婴儿死亡。美国几乎每个州都报告了活跃的疫情爆发。
威斯康星州卫生服务部门证实了这名婴儿的死亡，而纽约则记录了三十多年来首例已知的与麻疹相关的死亡病例。
疾病预防控制中心没有具体说明官方统计的六例死亡病例是哪些州造成的。
报告数据出现差异是因为美国卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪领导下的疾病预防控制中心追踪麻疹死亡人数的方式发生了变化。根据 9 月 4 日在该机构网站上发布的一份说明，该机构目前正在使用国家卫生统计中心 (NCHS) 的数据，这是跟踪一段时间内死亡率趋势的一种方法。
肯尼迪此前曾在没有证据的情况下辩称宾夕法尼亚州的两人死亡可能不是死于麻疹。据路透社报道，他要求疾病预防控制中心主任埃里卡施瓦茨不要将死亡人数计入疾病预防控制中心的官方统计中。路透社报道发表的第二天，疾病预防控制中心更改了麻疹死亡数据来源。
麻疹可通过麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹 (MMR) 疫苗预防，接种两剂后可提供约 97% 的保护。
美国本周可能会失去消除麻疹的地位，这一事态发展可能会进一步确定肯尼迪干预疫苗政策的遗产。失去这一称号将使美国与加拿大以及欧洲和亚洲的几个国家并列，而这些国家的麻疹此前已被消灭，但随后又卷土重来。

title_en: ‘Who will be held accountable?’: fatal Brooklyn building collapse devastates community
title_zh: “谁将承担责任？”：致命的布鲁克林建筑倒塌摧毁了社区
summary: New York City officials have confirmed at least eight casualties – six adults and two children – in the collapse Flatbush Ave in Flatbush, New York, stood still and in shock after a three-storey apartment building collapsed on Wednesday afternoon near a constr
summary_zh: 纽约市官员已确认，纽约州弗拉特布什大道的倒塌事故造成至少八人伤亡，其中包括六名成人和两名儿童。
body_en: New York City officials have confirmed at least eight casualties – six adults and two children – in the collapse
Flatbush Ave in Flatbush, New York , stood still and in shock after a three-storey apartment building collapsed on Wednesday afternoon near a construction site.
“The last time I saw something like this was when I went to work at 9/11,” Prudence Foster said.

Foster, a retired utility worker with ConEdison, has lived in the Brooklyn neighborhood most of her life and now lives on 19th Street – about a 20-minute drive from the wreckage. She heard helicopters on her way home on Wednesday and received a call from a friend about the building’s destruction.
Brooklyn building collapse kills at least two children and six adults, injuring 18
“I was glad the building didn’t blow up because of the gas lines,” Foster said. “Who is going to be held accountable for the loss of lives?”

Foster’s biggest concern is the residents left in the three buildings still standing and previously connected to the one that collapsed. Officials have also ordered the evacuation of all residents in those buildings during their investigation. Foster said the city should consider taking those buildings down before they also collapse.

Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor, addressed some of Foster’s, and other’s, concerns in a press conference Thursday. He confirmed officials are working with the department of buildings to investigate 100 other sites in New York City with connections to the building that gave way.
“If there is anyone or any entity operating in this city that bears responsibility for what happened, we will hold them fully accountable,” Mamdani said.
New York officials have confirmed at least eight casualties – six adults and two children – in the collapse. At least 18 other people have sustained non-fatal but serious injuries.

As of Thursday morning, the New York City police department rerouted several buses and blocked off Flatbush Avenue along Bedford Avenue and Clarendon Road to make space for responders and firefighters to continue their search for victims. Media teams, residents and employees at the small businesses from along the street all congregated on the sidewalk trying to get a view of the rubble.
“The city has come together to stand along those who are experiencing this hardship,” Mamdani said.
Red Cross set up a supply center at the Flatbush YMCA down the street from the collapse, providing temporary housing, social services and mental health support.

Brooklyn native James Williams works in the Chelsea Deli Grocery that sits directly across the street from the wreckage. He saw the apartment complex come down after hearing hours of loud banging from the construction.

From about 7am to 4pm, Williams said he heard noises that “sounded like a big gunshot”, from the construction site. He told reporters on Thursday that he was familiar with the workers since they came into the deli often for lunch.
“There were people trying to get out,” he said, coming close to tears. “I don’t even really want to think about that. I couldn’t even go over there to even help anybody.”
At about 4pm, Williams recalled smelling metal fumes and seeing bricks falling from the building. He watched the apartment building sink about two minutes afterward.

Ahmed Tigani, the department of buildings commissioner, said during the press conference that no violations or complaints in the area were reported in the building or the nearby construction but examinations will continue.
“If there is anyone or any entity operating in this cart that is responsible what happened, we will hold them fully accountable,” he said.
body_zh: 纽约市官员已确认倒塌事故造成至少八人伤亡，其中六名成人和两名儿童
周三下午，纽约州弗拉特布什的弗拉特布什大街一处建筑工地附近的一栋三层公寓楼倒塌后，人们惊魂未定。
“我最后一次看到这样的事情是在 9/11 去上班的时候，”普鲁登斯·福斯特说。
福斯特是康爱迪生公司的一名退休公用事业工人，她大部分时间都住在布鲁克林附近，现在住在第 19 街，距离残骸大约 20 分钟车程。周三，她在回家的路上听到了直升机的声音，并接到了朋友打来的关于大楼被毁的电话。
布鲁克林大楼倒塌造成至少两名儿童和六名成人死亡，18 人受伤
“我很高兴这座建筑没有因为煤气管道而爆炸，”福斯特说。 “谁来为生命损失负责？”
福斯特最担心的是三栋建筑中仍然矗立着的居民，并且之前与倒塌的那栋建筑相连。官员在调查期间还下令疏散这些建筑物内的所有居民。福斯特说，市政府应该考虑在这些建筑物倒塌之前将其拆除。
纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 在周四的新闻发布会上解决了福斯特和其他人的一些担忧。他证实，官员们正在与建筑部门合作，调查纽约市与倒塌大楼有关的其他 100 个地点。
马姆达尼说：“如果在这座城市运营的任何人或任何实体对所发生的事情负有责任，我们将追究他们的全部责任。”
纽约官员已确认倒塌事故造成至少八人伤亡——六名成人和两名儿童。至少还有 18 人受重伤，虽然没有死亡。
截至周四上午，纽约市警察局改变了几辆公交车的路线，并封锁了贝德福德大道和克拉伦登路沿线的弗拉特布什大道，为救援人员和消防员继续寻找受害者腾出空间。媒体团队、居民和沿街小企业的员工都聚集在人行道上，试图一睹废墟的风采。
马姆达尼说：“这座城市团结起来，与那些正在经历这种困难的人们站在一起。”
红十字会在倒塌地点附近的弗拉特布什基督教青年会 (Flatbush YMCA) 设立了一个供应中心，提供临时住房、社会服务和心理健康支持。
布鲁克林本地人詹姆斯·威廉姆斯在切尔西熟食杂货店工作，该杂货店就位于飞机残骸的街对面。在听到数小时的建筑巨响后，他看到公寓楼倒塌了。
威廉姆斯说，从早上 7 点到下午 4 点左右，他听到建筑工地传来“听起来像一声大枪声”的噪音。他周四告诉记者，他对工人们很熟悉，因为他们经常来熟食店吃午饭。
“有人试图逃走，”他说，几乎要哭了。 “我什至不想考虑这个。我什至无法去那里帮助任何人。”
下午 4 点左右，威廉姆斯回忆说，他闻到了金属烟雾的味道，还看到砖块从建筑物上掉下来。大约两分钟后，他看着公寓楼下沉。
建筑部专员艾哈迈德·蒂加尼(Ahmed Tigani)在新闻发布会上表示，该建筑或附近的建筑没有收到任何违规或投诉的报告，但检查将继续进行。
他说：“如果这辆购物车中的任何人或任何实体对所发生的事情负责，我们将追究他们的全部责任。”

title_zh: 皮特·赫格斯向在无名烈士墓附近训斥他的士兵颁发奖章
summary: ‘We love standards. Well done, Specialist’, the defense secretary writes following Veterans Day visit US politics live – latest updates The defense secretary, Pete Hegseth , on Thursday awarded a Joint Service Commendation Medal to the soldier who called out h
summary_zh: “我们喜欢标准。干得好，专家”，国防部长在退伍军人节访问美国政治直播后写道——最新动态
body_en: Pete Hegseth awards medal to soldier who reprimanded him near Tomb of the Unknown Soldier | Pete Hegseth
‘We love standards. Well done, Specialist’, the defense secretary writes following Veterans Day visit

The defense secretary, Pete Hegseth , on Thursday awarded a Joint Service Commendation Medal to the soldier who called out him and members of his staff after some in the group were heard laughing and talking near the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier during a Veterans Day visit.
“We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist,” Hegseth wrote in a social media post. “Carry on Patriots.” The post included a series of photos of Hegseth with the soldier.

A Pentagon official confirmed to CNN that Hegseth hosted members of the 3rd infantry regiment, known as the Old Guard, at the Pentagon “where he proudly awarded Specialist Iglesias the Joint Service Commendation Medal for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the unknown Soldier on November 11, 2026”.
The recognition came just one day after specialist Thomas Iglesias confronted members of Hegseth’s group at Arlington national cemetery.

Hegseth and his team were at the cemetery for a Veterans Day ceremony that was also attended by Donald Trump and JD Vance, who both laid wreaths at the memorial in honor of fallen soldiers and delivered remarks afterwards. Trump had called out Hegseth during his speech at the ceremony, saying he’s done a “fantastic job” in his role as defense secretary.

Hegseth was visiting the tomb alongside his wife, chief of staff Ricky Buria, deputy chief of staff Patrick Weaver, and senior adviser and deputy assistant Tami Radabaugh. The group had been posing for photographs in front of the tomb before they were caught laughing and talking.
Iglesias, who was patrolling the tomb at the time, abruptly stopped walking, turned toward the group and issued a warning.
“All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times,” Iglesias called out.

Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell addressed the incident in a statement: “The secretary and the entire department have always honored – and will always honor – the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe.

The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington national cemetery is one of the most sacred war memorials in the country, marking the final resting place of an unknown soldier who was killed in the first world war.

Soldiers from the Old Guard have maintained a round-the-clock watch over the tomb since 1948. Part of their responsibility includes enforcing strict standards of silence and respect, and correcting visitors whose behavior disrupts the solemn atmosphere.

The Joint Service Commendation Medal is awarded to members of the US armed forces who distinguish themselves by “meritorious achievement or service while serving in any specified activity”, according to the air force’s personnel center.
body_zh: 皮特·赫格斯向在无名烈士墓附近训斥他的士兵颁发奖章皮特·赫格斯
“我们喜欢标准。干得好，专家”，国防部长在退伍军人节访问后写道
周四，国防部长皮特·赫格赛斯 (Pete Hegseth) 在退伍军人节访问期间，在无名烈士墓附近听到了一些人在无名烈士墓附近大笑和交谈后，向这位向他和他的幕僚喊话的士兵授予了联合服役嘉奖奖章。
“我们热爱士兵。我们热爱标准。干得好，专家，”赫格斯在社交媒体帖子中写道。 “继续爱国者。”该帖子包含赫格斯与这名士兵的一系列照片。
一名五角大楼官员向 CNN 证实，赫格塞斯在五角大楼接待了被称为“老卫士”的第三步兵团成员，“他自豪地授予伊格莱西亚斯联合服役奖章，以表彰他于 2026 年 11 月 11 日在无名烈士墓中执行的职责”。
就在这一认可的一天前，专家托马斯·伊格莱西亚斯在阿灵顿国家公墓与赫格斯小组的成员对峙。
赫格斯和他的团队在墓地参加了退伍军人节仪式，唐纳德·特朗普和 JD·万斯也出席了仪式，他们都向纪念碑敬献了花圈，以纪念阵亡士兵，并在仪式后发表讲话。特朗普在仪式上发表讲话时称赞赫格斯塞斯，称他在担任国防部长期间做得“出色”。
赫格斯与他的妻子、幕僚长瑞奇·布里亚（Ricky Buria）、副幕僚长帕特里克·韦弗（Patrick Weaver）以及高级顾问兼副助理塔米·拉达博（Tami Radabaugh）一起参观了坟墓。这群人在坟墓前摆好姿势拍照，然后被发现有说有笑。
当时正在墓地巡逻的伊格莱西亚斯突然停下脚步，转身向众人发出警告。
“所有来访者将始终保持沉默和尊重的气氛，”伊格莱西亚斯喊道。
五角大楼首席发言人肖恩·帕内尔在一份声明中谈到了这一事件：“国务卿和整个部门一直尊重——并将永远尊重——我们的军人为保护美国安全而做出的牺牲。
阿灵顿国家公墓的无名烈士墓是该国最神圣的战争纪念馆之一，标志着在第一次世界大战中阵亡的无名战士的最后安息之地。
自 1948 年以来，老卫队士兵一直全天候守卫坟墓。他们的部分职责包括执行严格的沉默和尊重标准，并纠正破坏庄严气氛的访客行为。
据空军人事中心称，联合服役嘉奖奖章授予那些因“在任何特定活动中服役期间取得的功绩或服务”而脱颖而出的美国武装部队成员。

title_en: Witnesses describe the D.C. shooting that left 1 dead, 4 injured
title_zh: 目击者描述了导致 1 人死亡、4 人受伤的华盛顿枪击事件
summary: A gunman opened fire at a gym in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle Thursday morning. One person has been confirmed killed and four others injured. The gunman is dead, according to police.
summary_zh: 星期四早上，一名枪手向华盛顿特区洛根圆环的一家健身房开枪。已确认一人死亡，四人受伤。克
body_en: Local and federal law enforcement respond to reports of an active shooting on Thursday in Washington. Tom Brenner/AP hide caption
Busy morning crowds in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle ran for cover Thursday after a gunman opened fire at a local gym, VIDA Fitness, killing at least one person and injuring at least four others.

The gunman left the gym area, entered a nearby apartment building where he barricaded himself. Jeffery W. Carroll, the interim Police Chief of the Metropolitan Police Department, who briefed the public this morning, said at the time of the briefing that the shooter had shot himself.
A police spokeswoman later confirmed to NPR that the gunman died.

The gunman shot and killed one person inside the gym and injured another in the lobby or alley area of the building, Carroll said. The other three victims were shot across the street at a construction site, he said. One person remains in critical condition.
Carroll identified the gunman as a white male who had a conflict with the homeowners association of the apartment building.

The Logan Circle neighborhood sits about one mile north of the White House. The block where the shooting occurred, along 15th Street Northwest, is lined with apartment buildings, a church, coffee shops and restaurants.
Democrats plan to widen their probes of fatal ICE shootings

Residents around the area described a massive law enforcement presence, including FBI agents and SWAT teams, swarming the area minutes after gunshots rang out. Residents were sent emergency text messages ordering them to remain sheltered in place. That order was lifted at around 11:30 a.m.

The first call for help came in at 8 a.m. from people inside the gym, Carroll said. Officers and other emergency responders were on scene within 30 seconds, he said. Responders found one adult man who was shot inside the gym.
Witnesses on scene told NPR that VIDA requires visitors to tap in to gain access to the fitness area. Carroll told media he believes the gunman was a member.
Local and federal law enforcement respond to reports of an active shooting, Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, in Washington. Julia Demaree Nikhinson//AP hide caption
Tinbete Ermyas, an editor at NPR, was working out at the gym when the shooting started. He and other gym-goers became aware something was wrong when they heard "a very loud bang," Ermyas said.

"People kind of looked around at each other ... wondering what it was. Some people thought that maybe it was some weights that had been dropped. But it just sounded way too loud," he said. "The bang sort of shook everybody."

"That's when we realized that it was a shooting," he said. He and others ran off the gym floor through an emergency exit that led them to a laundry room. That's where for about 20 minutes, he and others hid until police came to escort them out.
Democrats want to stop Trump's arch, golf course and more. What are their options?
As they exited, they saw the body of the man who was shot.
"It was just laying there, just very bloodied and terrible. A guy that goes to the gym regularly. I see him every morning, just lying in a pool of blood. It was terrible," Ermyas said.

After the gunman barricaded himself in the apartment building, police tried for about an hour to get him to surrender safely. But Carroll said that while officers were engaging with the suspect, they heard a gunshot.
body_zh: 地方和联邦执法部门对周四华盛顿发生枪击事件的报道做出回应。汤姆·布伦纳/美联社隐藏标题栏
周四，一名枪手向当地一家健身房 VIDA Fitness 开枪，造成至少 1 人死亡、至少 4 人受伤，华盛顿特区洛根圆环 (Logan Circle) 早上忙碌的人群纷纷躲避。
枪手离开健身房，进入附近的一栋公寓楼，并将自己设在路障内。今天早上向公众通报情况的大都会警察局临时警察局长杰弗里·W·卡罗尔(Jeffery W. Carroll)在通报情况时表示，枪手开枪自杀。
警方发言人后来向 NPR 证实枪手已死亡。
卡罗尔说，枪手在体育馆内开枪打死一人，并在大楼大厅或小巷区域打伤另一人。他说，另外三名受害者是在街对面的一个建筑工地被枪杀的。一名人员仍处于危急状态。
卡罗尔确认枪手是一名白人男性，他与公寓楼房主协会发生冲突。
洛根圆环社区位于白宫以北约一英里处。枪击事件发生的街区位于西北第 15 街，两旁排列着公寓楼、教堂、咖啡馆和餐馆。
民主党计划扩大对 ICE 枪击事件的调查范围
该地区周围的居民称，枪声响起几分钟后，包括联邦调查局特工和特警队在内的大量执法人员涌入该地区。居民收到了紧急短信，命令他们留在原地避难。该命令于上午 11 点 30 分左右解除。
卡罗尔说，早上 8 点，健身房内的人第一次接到求救电话。他说，警察和其他紧急救援人员在 30 秒内就赶到了现场。救援人员发现一名成年男子在健身房内被枪击。
现场目击者告诉 NPR，VIDA 要求访客进入健身区。卡罗尔告诉媒体，他相信枪手是一名成员。
地方和联邦执法部门对 2026 年 11 月 12 日星期四在华盛顿发生的枪击事件报告做出回应。朱莉娅·德玛丽·尼金森//美联社隐藏标题栏
枪击事件发生时，NPR 编辑廷贝特·埃尔米亚斯 (Tinbete Ermyas) 正在健身房锻炼。埃尔米亚斯说，当他和其他去健身房的人听到“一声非常大的爆炸声”时，他们意识到出了问题。
“人们互相环顾四周……想知道那是什么。有些人认为可能是一些重物掉落了。但听起来太大声了，”他说。 “爆炸声震动了每个人。”
“那时我们意识到这是一起枪击事件，”他说。他和其他人从健身房地板上跑出，通过紧急出口进入洗衣房。他和其他人就在那里躲了大约20分钟，直到警察来护送他们出去。
民主党人希望阻止特朗普的拱门、高尔夫球场等。他们的选择是什么？
当他们离开时，他们看到了被枪杀的男子的尸体。
“它就躺在那里，血迹斑斑，非常可怕。一个经常去健身房的人。我每天早上都看到他，躺在血泊中。太可怕了，”埃尔米亚斯说。
枪手将自己锁在公寓楼内后，警方花了大约一个小时试图让他安全投降。但卡罗尔说，当警察与嫌疑人接触时，他们听到了枪声。

title_en: Mississippi elects Democrat Scott Colom to Senate in massive upset
title_zh: 密西西比州选举民主党人斯科特·科洛姆为参议院议员
summary: Colom's win is a boost to the Democratic Party as it seeks to gain a larger foothold in the South.
summary_zh: 科罗姆的胜利对民主党寻求在南方获得更大立足点的推动。
body_en: Mississippi voted blue, in a shock win for Democrats.

Democrat Scott Colom ousted Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in a state that went for President Donald Trump by 23 points in 2024. He will be the first Black senator elected in Mississippi since the Reconstruction era — and the first Democrat from the state headed to the Senate in 44 years.
Colom, a Democratic district attorney, ran a scrappy campaign that saw some national money and resources in the final stretch of the race.

Hyde-Smith was appointed to the Senate in 2018 and had since won election to the seat twice, but she faced attacks from Colom that she was out of touch and indifferent to rising grocery and gas prices during Trump’s second term.
National Democratic groups hadn't paid much attention to the Mississippi Senate race until an October surge of excitement for Colom drew late spending and attention.

Colom's win is a boost to the Democratic Party as it seeks to gain a larger foothold in the South and improve their standing with Black voters. It’s also a major vindication for Colom and other Southern Democrats who argued Mississippi had been neglected for far too long.
body_zh: 密西西比州投票支持蓝色，民主党意外获胜。
民主党人斯科特·科洛姆 (Scott Colom) 在该州以 23 个百分点的优势击败了参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯 (Cindy Hyde-Smith)，该州在 2024 年以 23 个百分点的优势支持唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 总统。他将成为密西西比州自重建时代以来第一位当选的黑人参议员，也是 44 年来该州第一位进入参议院的民主党参议员。
民主党地方检察官科洛姆进行了一场斗志旺盛的竞选活动，在竞选的最后阶段获得了一些国家资金和资源。
海德-史密斯于 2018 年被任命为参议员，此后两次赢得该席位的选举，但她面临科罗姆的攻击，称她在特朗普第二任期内对不断上涨的食品杂货和汽油价格漠不关心。
全国民主党团体并没有对密西西比州参议员竞选给予太多关注，直到十月份对科罗姆的兴奋激增吸引了后期的支出和关注。
科罗姆的胜利对民主党来说是一个推动，因为它寻求在南方获得更大的立足点并提高他们在黑人选民中的地位。这也是科洛姆和其他南方民主党人的一个重要证明，他们认为密西西比州被忽视太久了。

title_en: 2028 Dems: Don’t label me
title_zh: 2028 民主党：别给我贴标签
summary: Democrats with eyes on the White House are hoping to push the party past its long-running ideological war.
summary_zh: 着眼于白宫的民主党人希望推动该党摆脱长期的意识形态战争。
body_en: Democrats’ midterms sweep didn’t solve their ideological civil war — but a number of the party’s potential presidential contenders hope it lets them call a truce.
In the days since Democrats’ sweeping midterm victories, several likely White House aspirants have argued that their party’s factional feuding needs to take a backseat heading into 2028.

“What was clear, no matter where you go, [is that] people are frustrated,” Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro told reporters last weekend at Crooked Media’s post-election conference. “They're not thinking about whether this is about left or middle or right. They're thinking about how to get problems solved.”
“I don't know if the takeaway should be what ideology that people wanted. I think people want results,” Maryland Gov. Wes Moore said at the same event.

Democrats’ midterm tidal wave was powered more by voters’ anger at high costs and the Trump administration than by any one ideology. Candidates won tough races by positioning themselves not as progressives or moderates but as anti-Washington populists and pragmatists — some of them even scoring dual endorsements from both the moderate Blue Dog Democrats and progressive Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.).

“If you see … an elected leader spending valuable time duking it out on whose team won, moderate or progressive, they are missing the actual message of this election,” Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin, a moderate who campaigned hard for progressive Abdul El-Sayed, told POLITICO. “It’s about people who are wanting to work together as a team on issues like the American dream in the middle class.”Many of the party’s rising stars embraced an ethos like Shapiro’s “get stuff done” and, like Slotkin, called to reject progressive-versus-moderate politics in favor of combative candidates.

“It helps take away the most annoying question that has split our party, and that is the question of electability,” progressive Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) said in an interview last week. “It turns out that progressives were electable, and centrists were electable. The moderates were electable, and people who were affiliated with the DSA were electable.”

Now, as they pivot into 2028, Democrats are broadly seizing on last week’s results as license to avoid traditional labels as they look to appeal as widely as possible to voters more interested in easing the pinch in their pocketbooks than the political philosophy to which their leaders subscribe. Interviews and conversations with more than a dozen potential Democratic presidential candidates, advisers and operatives reveal that rhetorical shift is as much a rejection of the ideological litmus tests that dominated the 2020 primary as it is a calibration toward the dynamics that will drive the 2028 contest.

“We all lived through the purity tests,” said Adrienne Elrod, a Democratic strategist who advised Joe Biden in 2020, Kamala Harris in 2024 and Hillary Clinton’s 2016 run. “What people are now yearning for is authenticity. And they want a fighter and someone who can deliver more than someone who perfectly aligns with them ideologically.”

There are tells in the flurry of postelection memos from potential presidential contenders. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s team positioned her not as a progressive firebrand but as “one of the most effective voices in the country for America’s working class.” Teams behind Moore and Shapiro pushed messages of “common-sense governance” and “delivering results.”

“There has been a reckoning in the Democratic Party, and people in all lanes frankly have come to realize the government in Washington has not delivered for working-class people and they need to,” said Jeff Weaver, a Khanna adviser who managed Sanders’ 2016 presidential campaign.
Or, as one adviser to a potential candidate said: Voters “do not live in the binaries that a lot of political operatives do.”

While last Tuesday’s wave swept Democrats of all stripes into office, it also created openings for each wing of the party to argue that its vision is the way forward. That all but guarantees more proxy battles to come as the party moves from running a raft of candidates across diverse districts to selecting just one to try and win the White House.

The left has seized on strong performances by unabashedly progressive candidates to push Khanna and Ocasio-Cortez to run for president and Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) to challenge Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) for Senate majority leader.

Ravi Mangla, a spokesperson for the Working Families Party, said it’s “undeniable the populist candidates … can win in swing states that are going to be critical in 2028” — and the left lane is “wide open.”
But the centrist group Welcome argued in a new memo shared first with POLITICO that there’s a clear pathway for candidates willing to embrace a more moderate posture.

“In a very large field, you need a base to get you to 15, 20, 25 percent. And it’s very clear in the data you can get there with voters in the middle — center-left voters,” said Welcome co-founder Liam Kerr.

And even as he called for a primary that would battle test a diverse set of ideological views, Khanna, who co-chaired Sanders’ 2020 campaign, leaned into his liberal bona fides: “It would be an honor to be called a Bernie Sanders Democrat; I embrace being a New Deal Democrat with pride.”

“Obviously, I'm a progressive Democrat. I believe that the progressive vision is the best vision. But there should be someone who’s in the center or center-left. Then they can argue for their vision,” Khanna said. “And then it’s for the American people and the primary to decide.”
body_zh: 民主党的中期选举大获全胜并没有解决他们的意识形态内战，但该党的一些潜在总统候选人希望这能让他们休战。
民主党在中期选举中取得压倒性胜利后的几天里，几位可能入主白宫的人表示，进入 2028 年，他们党派的派系争斗需要退居二线。
“很明显，无论你走到哪里，人们都会感到沮丧，”宾夕法尼亚州州长乔什·夏皮罗上周末在 Crooked Media 的选举后会议上告诉记者。 “他们没有考虑这是左派、中间派还是右派的问题。他们正在考虑如何解决问题。”
“我不知道外卖是否应该是人们想要的意识形态。我认为人们想要结果，”马里兰州州长韦斯摩尔在同一活动中表示。
民主党的中期浪潮更多地是由选民对高成本和特朗普政府的愤怒推动的，而不是任何一种意识形态。候选人通过将自己定位为反华盛顿民粹主义者和实用主义者，而不是进步派或温和派，赢得了艰难的竞选——其中一些候选人甚至获得了温和派蓝狗民主党和进步派参议员伯尼·桑德斯（佛蒙特州）的双重支持。

“如果你看到......一位当选的领导人花费宝贵的时间来较量谁的团队获胜，无论是温和派还是进步派，他们都错过了这次选举的实际信息，”密歇根州参议员艾丽莎·斯洛特金（Elissa Slotkin）告诉《政治》杂志。 “这是关于那些希望作为一个团队在中产阶级的美国梦等问题上共同努力的人。”该党的许多后起之秀都拥护夏皮罗“把事情做好”这样的精神，并像斯洛特金一样，呼吁拒绝进步与温和的政治，转而支持好斗的候选人。
“这有助于消除导致我们党分裂的最恼人的问题，那就是选举能力问题，”进步派众议员罗·卡纳（加利福尼亚州民主党人）上周在接受采访时表示。 “事实证明，进步派可以当选，中间派也可以当选。温和派可以当选，隶属于 DSA 的人也可以当选。”
现在，随着进入 2028 年，民主党广泛抓住上周的结果作为避免传统标签的许可，因为他们希望尽可能广泛地吸引更感兴趣的是缓解钱包紧缩而不是其领导人所认同的政治哲学的选民。对十多名潜在的民主党总统候选人、顾问和工作人员的采访和对话表明，言论的转变既是对主导 2020 年初选的意识形态试金石的拒绝，也是对推动 2028 年竞选的动力的校准。
“我们都经历过纯度测试，”民主党策略师艾德丽安·埃尔罗德 (Adrienne Elrod) 说，她曾为 2020 年乔·拜登、2024 年卡马拉·哈里斯和 2016 年希拉里·克林顿竞选提供建议。 “人们现在渴望的是真实性。他们想要的是一个斗士，一个能够提供更多东西的人，而不是一个在意识形态上与他们完全一致的人。”
潜在总统候选人的一系列选举后备忘录中都透露出一些信息。众议员亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯的团队并未将她定位为进步的煽动者，而是“美国工人阶级最有效的声音之一”。摩尔和夏皮罗背后的团队传达了“常识性治理”和“交付成果”的信息。
曾负责桑德斯 2016 年总统竞选活动的卡纳顾问杰夫·韦弗 (Jeff Weaver) 表示：“民主党内部已经进行了清算，坦率地说，各派人士都已经意识到，华盛顿政府没有为工薪阶层人民带来好处，而他们需要这样做。”
或者，正如一位潜在候选人的顾问所说：选民“不像许多政治人物那样生活在二元体系中”。
虽然上周二的浪潮席卷了各派民主党人入主白宫，但它也为党内各派人士创造了机会，声称其愿景是前进的方向。随着该党从在不同选区竞选大量候选人转变为只选择一名候选人来试图赢得白宫，这几乎肯定会带来更多的代理权之争。
左翼利用毫不掩饰的进步候选人的强劲表现，推动卡纳和奥卡西奥-科尔特斯竞选总统，并推动参议员克里斯·范·霍伦（马里兰州民主党）挑战参议员查克·舒默（纽约州民主党）竞选参议院多数党领袖。
工作家庭党发言人拉维·曼格拉 (Ravi Mangla) 表示，“不可否认的是，民粹主义候选人……能够在 2028 年至关重要的摇摆州获胜”，而且左车道“敞开”。
但中间派团体Welcome在首先与POLITICO分享的一份新备忘录中表示，对于愿意采取更温和立场的候选人来说，有一条明确的途径。
“在一个非常大的领域，你需要一个基础才能让你的支持率达到 15%、20%、25%。数据非常清楚地表明，你可以通过中间选民（中左翼选民）达到目标，”Welcome 联合创始人利亚姆·克尔 (Liam Kerr) 说道。
桑德斯 2020 年竞选联合主席之一的卡纳呼吁举行一次初选，对多种意识形态观点进行较量，但他仍秉持着他的自由主义诚意：“被称为伯尼·桑德斯民主党人将是一种荣幸；我自豪地接受新政民主党人的身份。”
“显然，我是一名进步的民主党人。我相信进步的愿景是最好的愿景。但应该有人处于中间或中左翼。然后他们就可以为自己的愿景辩护，”卡纳说。 “然后由美国人民和初选来决定。”

title_en: A new crop of socialist mayors is coming to town. Will they deliver?

summary: Members of Democratic Socialists of America have a unique opportunity to fulfill campaign promises and group’s ideals As progressive candidates scored wins across the country last week, a historic number of socialists swept into power – in Congress, in state l

body_en: A new crop of socialist mayors is coming to town. Will they deliver? | Democratic socialism
Members of Democratic Socialists of America have a unique opportunity to fulfill campaign promises and group’s ideals
As progressive candidates scored wins across the country last week, a historic number of socialists swept into power – in Congress, in state legislatures and at the helm of American cities.

Democratic Socialists of America members Nithya Raman and Janeese Lewis George were elected to lead the second largest US city – Los Angeles – and the capital – Washington DC respectively. Two other young DSA members, David Morales and Yousef Rabhi, were elected mayors of Providence, Rhode Island, and Ann Arbor, Michigan. They will join a handful of socialist mayors in smaller cities, including Burlington, Vermont, and Irvine, California – as well as Zohran Mamdani , the democratic socialist mayor of New York, the largest city in the US.

Mamdani, who grew up politically within New York City’s DSA chapter and has become the insurgent leftist group ’s best known representative, was considered a long-shot candidate before his meteoric rise. He’s now one of the most popular politicians in the country and his election is widely credited with inspiring historic numbers of democratic socialists surging to office across the country and up and down the ballot.

Come January, the number of DSA members in Congress will have quadrupled (to eight), and more than 100 DSA-endorsed candidates will sit in local, state and national office. But DSA mayors, who have authority over more prosaic elements of governance, from garbage pickup to snow days , face a unique opportunity to prove to the public that the group’s ideals of affordability and inclusivity can improve the lives of working people – the central tenet of DSA’s vision.
“It’s the executive office, so the stakes are actually higher there,” said Eric Blanc, an assitant professor of labor studies at Rutgers University and DSA member.

“If politics cannot deliver on the block where you live, why would you trust it to deliver anywhere?” Mamdani told a gathering of mayors from around the world, on the sidelines of the United Nations general assembly earlier this fall . “If you are making a New Yorker’s life a little smoother, so too you are making their journey to believe in government’s ability to deliver for them.”

According to the New York Times, which covered the event, Mamdani made the remarks to fellow mayors to explain his fixation with potholes – his office says he has repaired more than 200,000 since taking office.

Similar to Mamdani, the incoming DSA mayors have run campaigns focused on affordability and practical improvement to people’s lives. Raman, an urban planner, has promised more housing and public transit improvements. Lewis George has campaigned on universal childcare, public housing and better protections for tenants. Morales has pitched affordable housing and called for corporations to contribute a larger share toward public education and city services. Rabhi has pledged to fight data centers and keep utilities affordable.

While his critics have generally focused on debates with little to do on municipal government, Mamdani has been focused on delivering on campaign promises such as a rent freeze , universal childcare and taxing the rich .

“Zohran already demonstrated proof of concept, contrary to all of the predictions of imminent collapse” of the city, Blanc said. “He has already demonstrated what democratic socialist governance can look like.”

“If others can follow this model, which is to take big fights against the rich and powerful, be out there proving to people that you can make their lives better, I think that is going to be what will help avoid some of the real difficulties of governing,” he added.

Katie Wilson, the mayor of Seattle and a self-identified democratic socialist – though not a DSA member – agreed. She called a mayor’s job “the best in the world” and noted that the office requires a mix of “the high and the low”.

“There’s big vision and ambitions and values, and then on the other hand a lot of the job is the real nitty-gritty of keeping the lights on,” she said. “It’s really important as socialists and progressives coming into office that we’re able to get those nitty-gritty details right, do the basics well.”

As a growing number of progressives have called on Democrats to “ deliver ”, following last week’s landslide wins, mayors will be the first to have to show results. Wilson said they should deliver on what is within their reach and maintain close working relationships with the grassroots organizers that helped them get elected.
“What people are affirming in voting for progressives and socialists in this moment, is that we believe in the power of government to improve people’s lives,” she said.
Even when the ability to deliver falls beyond their municipal authority, a mayor should show people “that you’re fighting for them”, she added.

“You’re not going to build socialism in one city ultimately, but how do you embody those values, and that vision, and take real, tangible steps toward socialistic policies, in a way that improves the daily lives of the residents of your city?”
body_zh: 新一批社会主义市长即将进驻该镇。他们会送货吗？ |民主社会主义
美国民主社会主义者的成员有独特的机会来实现竞选承诺和团体的理想
随着进步派候选人上周在全国各地取得胜利，历史上数量最多的社会主义者上台——在国会、州立法机构和美国城市的掌权者中。

美国民主社会主义者成员 Nithya Raman 和 Janeese Lewis George 分别当选为美国第二大城市洛杉矶和首都华盛顿特区的领导人。另外两名年轻的 DSA 成员戴维·莫拉莱斯 (David Morales) 和优素福·拉比 (Yousef Rabhi) 当选为罗德岛州普罗维登斯市和密歇根州安娜堡市的市长。他们将与佛蒙特州伯灵顿和加利福尼亚州欧文等小城市的少数社会主义市长以及美国最大城市纽约的民主社会主义市长佐赫兰·马姆达尼一起加入。
马姆达尼在纽约市 DSA 分会的政治生涯中长大，并已成为该叛乱左翼组织最著名的代表，在迅速崛起之前，他被认为是一个可能性不大的候选人。他现在是美国最受欢迎的政治家之一，人们普遍认为，他的当选鼓舞了全国各地以及选票上下的民主社会主义者数量创下历史新高。
到一月份，国会中 DSA 成员的数量将增加四倍（达到 8 名），超过 100 名 DSA 认可的候选人将在地方、州和国家办公室任职。但 DSA 市长们拥有对从垃圾收集到下雪天等更平常的治理要素的权力，他们面临着一个独特的机会，可以向公众证明，该组织的负担能力和包容性理想可以改善劳动人民的生活——这是 DSA 愿景的核心宗旨。
“这里是行政办公室，所以那里的风险实际上更高，”罗格斯大学劳工研究助理教授、DSA 成员埃里克·布兰克 (Eric Blanc) 说。
“如果政治不能在你居住的街区发挥作用，你为什么相信它能在任何地方发挥作用？”今年秋天早些时候，马姆达尼在联合国大会间隙向来自世界各地的市长们发表了讲话。 “如果你让纽约人的生活变得更加顺利，那么你也让他们相信政府有能力为他们提供服务。”
据报道该活动的《纽约时报》报道，马姆达尼向其他市长发表了上述言论，解释了他对坑洼的痴迷——他的办公室称，自上任以来，他已修复了超过 20 万个坑洼。
与马姆达尼类似，即将上任的 DSA 市长也开展了关注负担能力和实际改善人们生活的活动。城市规划师拉曼承诺进一步改善住房和公共交通。刘易斯·乔治一直致力于普及儿童保育、公共住房和更好地保护租户。莫拉莱斯提出了经济适用房的主张，并呼吁企业为公共教育和城市服务贡献更大的份额。拉比承诺打击数据中心并确保公用事业负担得起。
虽然他的批评者普遍关注与市政府无关的辩论，但马姆达尼一直专注于兑现竞选承诺，例如冻结租金、全民儿童保育和对富人征税。
布兰克说，“佐兰已经展示了概念验证，这与所有关于该城市即将崩溃的预测相反”。 “他已经展示了民主社会主义治理的样子。”
“如果其他人能够效仿这种模式，即与富人和有权势的人进行激烈的斗争，向人们证明你可以让他们的生活变得更好，我认为这将有助于避免一些真正的治理困难，”他补充道。
西雅图市长凯蒂·威尔逊（Katie Wilson）自称是民主社会主义者（尽管不是 DSA 成员），对此表示同意。她称市长的工作是“世界上最好的”，并指出这个办公室需要“高低”的混合体。
“有远大的愿景、雄心和价值观，而另一方面，很多工作的真正本质是维持运转，”她说。 “对于上任的社会主义者和进步人士来说，我们能够正确处理这些细节，做好基础工作，这一点非常重要。”
随着越来越多的进步人士呼吁民主党“兑现承诺”，继上周取得压倒性胜利后，市长们将是第一个必须展示结果的人。威尔逊表示，他们应该实现力所能及的目标，并与帮助他们当选的基层组织者保持密切的工作关系。
她说：“此时此刻，人们投票支持进步派和社会主义者所确认的是，我们相信政府有能力改善人民的生活。”
她补充说，即使交付能力超出了市政当局的能力，市长也应该向人们表明“你正在为他们而战”。
“你最终不会在一个城市建设社会主义，但如何体现这些价值观和愿景，并采取真正、切实的步骤实现社会主义政策，从而改善城市居民的日常生活？”

title_en: Biden says he wouldn't have run in 2024 if he knew about his cancer
title_zh: 拜登表示，如果他知道自己患有癌症，他就不会参加 2024 年竞选
summary: The former president also called his debate performance “not very consequential” in an interview with People magazine.
summary_zh: 这位前总统在接受《人物》杂志采访时还称他的辩论表现“不是很重要”。
body_en: Former President Joe Biden would not have run for reelection in 2024 if he had known about his cancer, he said in an interview released Wednesday in which he also sought to downplay the historic debate performance that helped end his political career.

"If I had known that I was feeling lousy because I had cancer, I would have not gone forward because I don't think an 80-year-old man with cancer should be running," he said in the interview with People magazine , which was conducted last week following Democrats’ big midterm wins and ahead of his upcoming memoir’s release.

The former president announced his diagnosis — Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer — in May 2025, just four months after leaving the White House. It triggered an outpouring of public support — but it also raised questions about how doctors failed to catch the cancer earlier and whether it might have contributed to Biden’s apparent decline toward the end of his term.

“I think it’s very sad, actually. I’m surprised that it wasn’t, you know, the public wasn’t notified a long time ago because to get to [a Gleason score of] 9, that’s a long time,” President Donald Trump told reporters shortly after Biden’s announcement.
Prior to his diagnosis, Biden hadn’t been screened for prostate cancer since 2014 . U.S. guidelines have long recommended that men shouldn't be screened for the cancer once they hit their 70s.
Biden also downplayed his poor June 2024 debate performance against Trump that contributed to his exit from the Democratic ticket a month later.

“To me, it was not very consequential,” he said. “First of all, I thought there would be another debate, which there wasn’t. But notwithstanding the fact that there wasn’t another debate, it didn’t disturb me because it wasn’t consequential.”

Biden’s son, Hunter, has said he believes the cancer was responsible for the performance. His weak showing on the debate stage led to mounting calls within his party for him to withdraw, an effort eventually backed by longtime friends and allies such as former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi .

The former president’s memoir , “Promise Me, America,” will go on sale next week. Biden wrote Sunday on X that the cancer meant he “won’t be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped.” But he still feels sharp, he told the magazine.
“I’m not saying I’ll live forever, but the point is that, you know, I have all my faculties, I have access to all the things I had before and, you know, I feel good,” he said.
body_zh: 前总统乔·拜登在周三发布的采访中表示，如果他知道自己患有癌症，他就不会在 2024 年竞选连任。他在采访中还试图淡化导致其政治生涯终结的历史性辩论表现。
“如果我知道我因为得了癌症而感觉很糟糕，我就不会继续前进，因为我认为一个患有癌症的 80 岁老人不应该参加竞选，”他在上周民主党取得中期选举大胜之后、他即将出版的回忆录之前接受《人物》杂志采访时说道。
这位前总统于 2025 年 5 月，即离开白宫仅四个月后，宣布了自己的诊断结果——第四期转移性前列腺癌。它引发了公众的大量支持，但也引发了人们的疑问：医生为何未能更早发现癌症，以及这是否可能导致拜登在任期结束时的明显衰落。
“事实上，我认为这非常令人难过。令我惊讶的是，你知道，公众很久以前就没有得到通知，因为要达到[格里森分数]9，那是很长一段时间，”唐纳德·特朗普总统在拜登宣布这一消息后不久告诉记者。
在确诊之前，拜登自 2014 年以来就没有接受过前列腺癌筛查。美国指南长期以来一直建议男性在 70 多岁时就不应接受癌症筛查。
拜登还淡化了他在 2024 年 6 月对阵特朗普的辩论中糟糕的表现，这导致他在一个月后退出民主党竞选。
“对我来说，这并不是很重要，”他说。 “首先，我以为还会有另一场辩论，但事实并非如此。尽管事实上没有另一场辩论，但这并没有打扰我，因为这并不重要。”
拜登的儿子亨特表示，他认为癌症是造成这一表现的原因。他在辩论舞台上的疲软表现导致党内要求他退出的呼声越来越高，这一努力最终得到了前众议院议长南希·佩洛西等长期朋友和盟友的支持。
这位前总统的回忆录《答应我，美国》将于下周发售。拜登周日在 X 上写道，癌症意味着他“无法像我希望的那样就我的书进行多次对话”。但他告诉杂志，他仍然感觉很敏锐。
“我并不是说我会永远活下去，但重点是，你知道，我拥有我所有的能力，我可以获得我以前拥有的所有东西，而且，你知道，我感觉很好，”他说。

title_en: USPS adds permanent postage surcharge, citing higher fuel costs
title_zh: 美国邮政总局以燃油成本上涨为由​​增加永久邮费附加费
summary: Still swimming in red ink, the USPS said it will raise some postage prices in 2027 to offset elevated fuel costs.
summary_zh: 美国邮政局 (USPS) 仍处于亏损状态，表示将在 2027 年提高部分邮资价格，以抵消燃油成本上涨的影响。
body_en: USPS says it will make its postage fuel surcharge permanent in 2027 as diesel prices soar - CBS News
The U.S. Postal Service on Thursday said it will permanently raise postage rates next year to cover higher fuel costs.

The USPS will make a temporary 8% surcharge on select postage prices, originally introduced in April , permanent in 2027, and also tack on a 3% price increase. The USPS Board of Governors, which oversees the agency's policies, approved the 11% hike, according to the USPS.
The changes will take effect on Jan. 17, 2027.

"The USPS governors believe these new rates will keep the Postal Service competitive while providing the agency with much needed revenue as it continues to struggle with financial issues," the agency said in a statement .
The agency will reevaluate the surcharge in July 2027 based on fuel prices in the first half of the year.
The USPS also said it would increase domestic shipping service costs by an average of 5.9% for Priority Mail service, Priority Mail Express, USPS Ground Advantage and Parcel Select.

In addition, international rates will rise by an average of 7.9% for Priority Mail Express International, Priority Mail International, First-Class Package International Service and International Priority Airmail.

Like other shipping and delivery companies, the USPS has faced sharply higher costs this year due to soaring diesel prices, which have spiked alongside global oil costs driven up by the war in Iran . The national average price of diesel was $6.10 per gallon on Thursday, up from $3.76 a year ago, according to AAA .

The USPS, which is self-financed, has for years struggled with high costs and dwindling mail volume. The agency on Tuesday reported a $6.5 billion loss for fiscal year 2026, down from a $9 billion loss last year. To stanch the bleeding, the Postal Service has implemented a 10-year plan to reduce expenses and restore profitability.

The U.S. Postal Service was established in 1775, with Benjamin Franklin serving as the first postmaster general. As an independent agency, the Postal Service is run by the USPS Board of Governors, which includes the postmaster general and a deputy postmaster general.

美国邮政服务周四表示，明年将永久提高邮资费率，以支付更高的燃料成本。
USPS 将对部分邮资价格临时加收 8% 的附加费（最初于 4 月推出），并于 2027 年永久生效，同时价格还会上涨 3%。据 USPS 称，负责监督该机构政策的 USPS 理事会批准了 11% 的加息。
这些变更将于 2027 年 1 月 17 日生效。
该机构在一份声明中表示：“美国邮政总局州长认为，这些新费率将保持邮政服务的竞争力，同时为该机构提供急需的收入，因为该机构继续与财务问题作斗争。”
该机构将于2027年7月根据上半年燃油价格重新评估附加费。
USPS 还表示，Priority Mail 服务、Priority Mail Express、USPS Ground Advantage 和 Parcel Select 的国内运输服务成本将平均增加 5.9%。
此外，Priority Mail Express International、Priority Mail International、First-Class Package International Service 和 International Priority Airmail 的国际费率将平均上涨 7.9%。
与其他运输和快递公司一样，由于柴油价格飙升，美国邮政今年面临成本大幅上升的问题，而柴油价格随着伊朗战争推高的全球石油成本而飙升。根据 AAA 的数据，周四全国柴油平均价格为每加仑 6.10 美元，高于一年前的 3.76 美元。
美国邮政局是自筹资金的，多年来一直在与高成本和不断减少的邮件量作斗争。该机构周二公布 2026 财年亏损 65 亿美元，低于去年的 90 亿美元亏损。为了止血，邮政服务实施了一项十年计划，以减少开支并恢复盈利能力。
美国邮政局成立于 1775 年，本杰明·富兰克林担任第一任邮政局长。作为一个独立机构，邮政服务由 USPS 理事会管理，其中包括邮政局长和副邮政局长。

body_en: 1 killed, 4 injured in shooting in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle neighborhood; suspect is dead - CBS News
Five people were shot, including one who died, as a gunman opened fire in and outside a gym in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle neighborhood on Thursday morning, police said.

Multiple law enforcement sources identified the shooter as Matthew Lambert, a doctor who lived in an apartment unit above Logan Circle's Vida Fitness. Jeffrey Carroll, the interim chief of the Metropolitan Police Department, later confirmed the shooter's identity and said he was 55 years old.

Carroll said Lambert barricaded himself inside his apartment after the shooting. He spoke with negotiators for about an hour before shooting himself, Carroll said. Police later confirmed he died at the scene, where a shotgun, a rifle and a handgun were recovered.

Carroll said there were five victims, not counting the shooter. One is deceased, one is in critical condition and three have non-life-threatening injuries. The injured victims have been transported to area hospitals, Carroll said.

The victim who was killed was identified as James Stuart, a 46-year-old D.C. resident. Police said he was the manager of the building where the shooting occurred and investigators believe he was specifically targeted because of the gunman's long-running conflict with the building's homeowners association.
The four people hospitalized are two men and two women. They have not been publicly identified and it was not immediately clear if they were specifically targeted or shot at random.
Carroll said police received a call for the shooting just before 8 a.m. and that authorities responded within 30 seconds.

Stuart was shot in the gym. Other victims included members of a construction crew across the street and a person in the lobby or alley outside the gym, Carroll said. The suspect is believed to have used all three firearms at some point, Carroll said.
Police said they were not sure how the shooter obtained the three guns recovered in his apartment, noting none were registered to him in Washington, D.C.

CBS News national security correspondent Nicole Sganga says it appears the suspect opened fire in and outside Vida Fitness, then retreated into a parking garage and ascended into the apartment building before barricading himself in a unit on the seventh floor, where police say he lived.
Carroll said the four victims who were hospitalized were shot at by the gunman after he had retreated to his apartment, and that he fired at them from his patio balcony.

Police believe the suspect used the handgun while in the gym and the rifle when he was on the balcony. He said the shotgun was used "at the end of the incident," but did not specify if that was the gun the shooter used to kill himself.

Carroll said a fire also was set inside the building at some point during the incident. The suspect broke the gas line in his apartment's fireplace and there was also gasoline and other flammable materials in the apartment, Carroll disclosed. The building's sprinklers went off and firefighters arrived shortly after, containing the fire.

Carroll said the initial shooting of the five victims unfolded within a time period of about five minutes. Gunshots continued to be heard for the better part of two hours, while officers with the Metro Police Department negotiated with the suspect. Carroll said the suspect fired through the apartment door at police on two occasions. While on the phone with negotiators, the suspect shot himself, Carroll said.
After hearing the gunshot, officers forced entry into the apartment, where they found the suspect suffering from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Carroll did not say where the suspect shot himself.

Joel Braithwaite, an attorney who represented Lambert, told reporters on Thursday that he was shocked by the shooting, saying, "The person I knew as a client, Dr. Matt Lambert, was an emergency room physician, someone that was in the business of healing people and helping them on a pretty bad day in their life."

According to the Washington Sun's Michael Brice-Saddler, who spoke to the gunman last year concerning his ongoing issues with his building management, Lambert worked as an emergency room doctor for two decades before moving on to working in health care IT.
Police say suspect had conflict with homeowners association
Carroll said most of the conversation between the shooter and the negotiators was centered around the conflicts the shooter had with the building's homeowners association.
body_zh: 华盛顿特区洛根圆环附近发生枪击事件，造成 1 人死亡、4 人受伤；嫌疑人已死亡 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
警方称，周四上午，一名枪手在华盛顿特区洛根圆环附近的一家健身房内外开枪，导致五人中枪，其中一人死亡。
多名执法部门消息人士确认，枪手是马修·兰伯特 (Matthew Lambert)，他是一名医生，住在洛根圈 (Logan Circle) 维达健身中心 (Vida Fitness) 楼上的公寓里。大都会警察局临时局长杰弗里·卡罗尔后来证实了枪手的身份，并称他今年 55 岁。
卡罗尔说，枪击事件发生后，兰伯特将自己关在公寓里。卡罗尔说，他在开枪自杀前与谈判代表进行了大约一个小时的交谈。警方后来证实他当场死亡，并发现了一把猎枪、一支步枪和一把手枪。
卡罗尔说，不包括枪手在内，有五名受害者。 1人死亡，1人情况危急，3人伤势不危及生命。卡罗尔说，受伤者已被送往地区医院。
被杀的受害者被确认为 46 岁的华盛顿居民詹姆斯·斯图尔特 (James Stuart)。警方称，他是发生枪击事件的大楼的经理，调查人员认为，由于枪手与大楼房主协会的长期冲突，他成为特别目标。
住院的四人是两男两女。他们的身份尚未被公开，也不清楚他们是否是专门针对的或随机射击的。
卡罗尔说，上午 8 点左右，警方接到了枪击事件的报警电话，当局在 30 秒内做出了回应。
斯图尔特在健身房被枪杀。卡罗尔说，其他受害者包括街对面的建筑工人和健身房外大厅或小巷中的一个人。卡罗尔说，据信嫌疑人在某个时候使用了所有三把枪。
警方表示，他们不确定枪手是如何获得在他的公寓中发现的三把枪的，并指出没有一把枪是他在华盛顿特区登记的。
哥伦比亚广播公司国家安全记者妮可·斯甘加 (Nicole Sganga) 表示，嫌疑人似乎在维达健身中心内外开枪，然后撤退到停车场，并爬进公寓楼，然后将自己关在七楼的一个单元里，警方称他居住在那里。
卡罗尔说，住院的四名受害者在枪手撤退到自己的公寓后被枪杀，他从露台阳台向他们开枪。
警方认为嫌疑人在健身房时使用手枪，在阳台上使用步枪。他说这把猎枪是在“事件结束时”使用的，但没有具体说明这是否是枪手用来自杀的枪。
卡罗尔说，事件发生期间，大楼内还起火。卡罗尔透露，嫌疑人打破了公寓壁炉中的煤气管道，公寓内还有汽油和其他易燃材料。大楼的洒水装置关闭，消防队员不久后赶到，控制住了火势。
卡罗尔说，五名受害者的最初枪击事件发生在大约五分钟的时间内。在两个小时的大部分时间里，枪声持续不断，而地铁警察局的警官正在与嫌疑人进行谈判。卡罗尔说，嫌疑人两次从公寓门向警察开枪。卡罗尔说，嫌疑人在与谈判人员通电话时开枪自杀。
听到枪声后，警察强行进入公寓，发现嫌疑人身上有自伤枪伤。卡罗尔没有透露嫌疑人在哪里开枪自杀。
兰伯特的代理律师乔尔·布雷思韦特周四告诉记者，他对这起枪击事件感到震惊，他说：“我认识的客户马特·兰伯特医生是一名急诊室医生，他的工作是治愈人们并帮助他们度过人生中非常糟糕的一天。”
《华盛顿太阳报》的迈克尔·布里斯-萨德勒 (Michael Brice-Saddler) 去年与枪手谈论了他在建筑管理方面持续存在的问题，据他介绍，兰伯特在从事医疗保健 IT 工作之前，曾担任急诊室医生二十年。
警方称嫌疑人与房主协会有冲突
卡罗尔表示，枪手和谈判代表之间的大部分对话都围绕枪手与大楼房主协会的冲突展开。

title_en: What's a Honey Trap? The spy tactic that helped topple Jensen Huang
title_zh: 什么是蜜糖陷阱？帮助推翻黄仁勋的间谍策略
summary: Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, the leading AI chipmaker, resigned after admitting an extramarital affair with a woman the U.S. says is a Chinese spy. This espionage tactic is known as a honey trap.
summary_zh: 领先的人工智能芯片制造商英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在承认与一名被美国认定为中国间谍的女性发生婚外情后辞职。钍
body_en: What’s a Honey Trap? The spy tactic that helped topple Jensen Huang Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, the leading AI chipmaker, resigned after admitting an extramarital affair with a woman the U.S. says is a Chinese spy. This espionage tactic is known as a honey trap.

A screengrab from CTI video footage obtained November 9, 2026 shows a woman identified by Reuters as Alice Huang after comparison with a photograph obtained separately, attending a dinner with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (in black) at a restaurant in Taipei, Taiwan on May 22, 2025. CTI via Reuters hide caption

One of the world's oldest spy tactics appears to have helped topple one of the world's richest men. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday amid revelations that he had an affair with a female client that U.S. intelligence identified as a Chinese spy, according to the New York Times.

NPR has not independently confirmed the reporting by the Times, which said Huang also had an unrelated affair with a company executive who reported to him. The Chinese government has called the accusation of spying, "nothing but smears against China."

Using a romantic relationship to gather intelligence from foreigners – known as a honey trap – has a long history in China and beyond. The Chinese Ministry of State Security, the country's main civilian intelligence agency, routinely tries to recruit women and occasionally men for honey traps, according to former CIA officers and other U.S. officials familiar with Chinese spy craft.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down amid alleged spy scandal

Some target businessmen for industrial espionage or to gain insights into the economic and political strategy of foreign governments. Peter Mattis , a former CIA counter-intelligence analyst, said honey traps also serve as influence operations with spies trying to gain enough trust to shape the target's thinking about China.

"The biggest thing here that we should pay attention to is that the Ministry of State Security celebrates a tradition of getting inside the enemy's decision-making," said Mattis, president of the Jamestown Foundation , a national security think tank in Washington, D.C., that focuses on America's geopolitical rivals.

Nicholas Eftimiades , who spent more than 34 years with the CIA and Defense Intelligence Agency and now teaches at Penn State, said the honey trap is just one tactic among many that use ordinary Chinese citizens to gather information at home and abroad.

"Unlike the CIA, or MI6 or any of the other Western services, China has a 'whole of society approach,'" said Eftimiades, the author of Chinese Intelligence Operations: An Analysis of the People's Republic of China's Intelligence Services. "Chinese law supports this. The National Intelligence Law of 2017 requires citizens to cooperate with intelligence collection efforts."

The Chinese government has employed honey traps in the United States and elsewhere in the West. In the 2010s, Christine Fang worked as a political fundraiser in California where she developed a physical relationship with Democrat Rep. Eric Swalwell before and after he became a congressman.
The FBI warned Swalwell they thought Fang was a spy. He denied doing anything wrong and she fled back to China.
An LA-area mayor acted as an agent for China. Experts say it's part of a pattern

In the 1980s and 1990s, the FBI paid Katrina Leung – a Los Angeles businesswoman – $1.7 million over 18 years to spy on China. However, Leung had affairs with two FBI agents and the bureau later determined she was a double-agent.

The most remarkable honey trap case dates to the 1960s, when a young French diplomat began a nearly two-decade affair with a male Peking opera performer, whom he thought was a woman. The story inspired the play and movie, M Butterfly .

The woman implicated in the Nvidia case, Alice Huang, is a Chinese businesswoman whose company, Megaspeed, was a major buyer of advanced chips from Nvidia. The Times reported the U.S. had her under surveillance and learned of her connections to Chinese state security through her communications.

The logo of data center company Megaspeed International is pictured at its office in the Ocean Financial Centre in Singapore on November 10, 2026. The woman accused of spying for China during an affair with Jensen Huang, head of US artificial intelligence chip titan Nvidia, has been named in media reports as tech executive Alice Huang, who has reportedly been a top figure at Singapore-based company. Taryn Ng/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

Desmond Shum, a Hong Kong businessman and former China insider, says Alice Huang doesn't fit the usual profile in these cases. She appears to be what the Chinese call a "white glove" – or front-person for multi-billion-dollar commercial deals, which Shum says could have insulated her from the Ministry of State Security.
body_zh: 什么是蜜糖陷阱？帮助推翻黄仁勋的间谍策略 领先的人工智能芯片制造商英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在承认与一名美国称其为中国间谍的女性发生婚外情后辞职。这种间谍策略被称为“美人计”。
2026 年 11 月 9 日获得的 CTI 视频片段的屏幕截图显示，路透社在与单独获得的照片进行比较后确认，一名女性名叫 Alice Huang，她于 2025 年 5 月 22 日在台湾台北的一家餐厅与 Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋（黑衣）共进晚餐。CTI 来自路透社 隐藏标题栏
世界上最古老的间谍策略之一似乎帮助推翻了世界上最富有的人之一。据《纽约时报》报道，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋周四辞职，原因是他与一名被美国情报部门认定为中国间谍的女性客户有染。
NPR 尚未独立证实《纽约时报》的报道，该报道称黄还与向他汇报的一名公司高管有不相关的婚外情。中国政府称这一间谍指控“只不过是对中国的抹黑”。
利用浪漫关系从外国人那里收集情报（称为美人计）在中国及其他地区有着悠久的历史。据前中央情报局官员和其他熟悉中国间谍活动的美国官员透露，中国主要的民事情报机构国家安全部经常试图招募女性，有时甚至招募男性来设置“美人计”。
英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因涉嫌间谍丑闻辞职
有些人以商人为目标进行工业间谍活动或了解外国政府的经济和政治战略。前中央情报局反情报分析师彼得·马蒂斯表示，美人计也是一种影响力行动，间谍试图获得足够的信任来塑造目标对中国的看法。
华盛顿特区国家安全智囊团詹姆斯敦基金会主席马蒂斯表示，“我们最应该注意的是，国家安全部推崇深入敌人决策的传统。”该基金会专注于美国的地缘政治竞争对手。
尼古拉斯·埃夫蒂亚德斯 (Nicholas Eftimiades) 在中央情报局和国防情报局工作了超过 34 年，现在宾夕法尼亚州立大学任教，他表示，美人计只是利用普通中国公民收集国内外信息的众多策略之一。
“与中央情报局、军情六处或任何其他西方机构不同，中国采取‘全社会方法’，”《中国情报行动：中华人民共和国情报部门分析》一书的作者埃夫蒂亚德斯说。 “中国法律支持这一点。2017年的《国家情报法》要求公民配合情报收集工作。”
中国政府在美国和西方其他地方设置了陷阱。 2010 年代，克里斯汀·方 (Christine Fang) 在加利福尼亚州担任政治筹款人，在民主党众议员埃里克·斯瓦尔韦尔 (Eric Swalwell) 成为国会议员之前和之后，她与他建立了肉体关系。
联邦调查局警告斯沃尔韦尔，他们认为方是间谍。他否认做错任何事，她逃回中国。
洛杉矶地区的一位市长充当了中国的代理人。专家称这是模式的一部分
在 20 世纪 80 年代和 90 年代，联邦调查局 (FBI) 向洛杉矶女商人卡特里娜·梁 (Katrina Leung) 在 18 年的时间里支付了 170 万美元，让她监视中国。然而，梁与两名联邦调查局特工有染，该局后来确定她是双重间谍。
最引人注目的美人计案件可以追溯到 20 世纪 60 年代，当时一名年轻的法国外交官与一名京剧男演员开始了近两年的恋情，他认为该男演员是一名女性。这个故事启发了戏剧和电影《蝴蝶君》。
与英伟达案有关的女性爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 是一位中国女商人，她的公司 Megaspeed 是英伟达先进芯片的主要买家。 《泰晤士报》报道称，美国对她进行监视，并通过她的通讯了解到她与中国国家安全部门的关系。

数据中心公司 Megaspeed International 的徽标于 2026 年 11 月 10 日在新加坡海洋金融中心的办公室拍摄。媒体报道称，这名被指控在与美国人工智能芯片巨头英伟达 (Nvidia) 负责人黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 发生关系期间为中国从事间谍活动的女性是技术高管 Alice Huang，据报道，她是这家新加坡公司的高层人物。 Taryn Ng/法新社，来自盖蒂图片社 隐藏标题栏
香港商人、前中国内部人士德斯蒙德·岑表示，黄爱丽在这些案件中不符合通常的形象。她似乎是中国人所说的“白手套”，即数十亿美元商业交易的代表人物，沉向洋表示，这可以让她免受国家安全部的影响。

title_en: Democrats launch Nvidia investigation, write scathing letter on Huang’s ‘scheme’ with Trump
title_zh: 民主党发起英伟达调查，针对黄仁勋与特朗普的“计划”写了一封措辞严厉的信
summary: This Congressional investigation into Nvidia's China sales and its dealings with Trump is the second one, so far, since news of the alleged spy affair broke.
summary_zh: 自涉嫌间谍事件的消息传出以来，国会对英伟达在中国的销售及其与特朗普的交易进行了第二次调查
body_en: Democrats launch Nvidia investigation, write scathing letter on Huang's 'scheme' with Trump | TechCrunch

Democrats on Thursday opened an inquiry into how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China. Earlier on Thursday, the company ousted its CEO Jensen Huang . He also agreed to testify to a different set of Republican-led Congressional committees.

Huang was removed from the company he founded after he confessed to an extramarital affair amid reports of a relationship with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. (He has since been accused of having more affairs , with Nvidia employees.)

The alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that U.S. officials suspect of helping route advanced Nvidia chips into China. The Democratic inquiry comes from Rep. Richard Neal (D-Mass.), the top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, and Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee. As the minority party, they can ask questions but can’t compel answers.
Their humdinger of a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick asks the department to preserve records about an arrangement they find questionable and, they allege, illegal.

“The scheme worked like this,” as the letter describes it. President Trump agreed to sales of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China as long as the chips, manufactured by Taiwan, were first shipped to the United States. On arriving, Trump added a tariff “effectively taking a cut of Nvidia’s sales to China through what appears to be an unconstitutional export tax system,” the letter said. Then the Commerce Department, under Lutnick, issued an export license.

By the way, the deal between Trump and Nvidia to share revenue was public. In August 2025, Nvidia and AMD both agreed to share 15% of their revenue from chip sales to China with the U.S. government as part of a deal to secure export licenses, the AP reported at the time.

But the letter questions why Lutnick continued to allow Megaspeed to buy chips even after he was reportedly informed by US intelligence of their suspicions of Alice Huang and of Jensen Huang’s relationship with her. It questionswhy the department reportedly green-lit other Asian companies to buy Nvidia chips “with no physical presence at their listed addresses.” So the inquiry is aimed at the administration, not just Nvidia and Huang.

The letter also questions how Nvidia’s donations to Trump’s projects factored in. It notes that the export deal was approved after Trump learned of “Mr. Huang’s compromised position” in sleeping with an alleged spy, and after Nvidia donated $26 million toward Trump’s projects, including the ballroom. It appears to be asking if Trump used his knowledge of the affair to secure donations from Nvidia.

Interestingly, in a “60 Minutes” interview with President Trump that aired on Sunday, he mentioned how he and his team had threatened an unnamed AI exec with jail , and after that, the exec “totally changed.”

This Congressional investigation into Nvidia’s China sales and its dealings with Trump is the second one, so far, since news of the alleged spy affair broke. The Republican-led group involves leaders from the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the House Intelligence Committee. That group has demanded that Huang come to them and testify in a closed-door session. They had threatened to subpoena him if he didn’t voluntarily agree. On Thursday, after his resignation, he agreed.

body_zh: 民主党发起英伟达调查，针对黄仁勋与特朗普的“计划”写了一封措辞严厉的信TechCrunch
民主党周四对特朗普政府如何处理英伟达向中国销售芯片展开调查。周四早些时候，该公司罢免了首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang)。他还同意向共和党领导的另一组国会委员会作证。
黄先生因与一名被指控为中国间谍的女性发生关系的报道而承认婚外情，随后被从他创办的公司中除名。 （此后他被指控与 Nvidia 员工有更多的风流韵事。）
被指控的中国间谍爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 是 Nvidia 客户 Megaspeed 的高管，该公司是一家总部位于新加坡的公司，美国官员怀疑该公司帮助将先进的 Nvidia 芯片运往中国。民主党调查由众议院筹款委员会民主党领袖理查德·尼尔（马萨诸塞州民主党议员）和参议院财政委员会民主党领袖参议员罗恩·怀登（俄勒冈州民主党人）发起。作为少数党，他们可以提出问题，但不能强迫答案。
他们给商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克写了一封信，要求商务部保留有关他们认为有问题且非法的安排的记录。
正如信中所描述的那样，“这个计划是这样运作的”。特朗普总统同意向中国出售英伟达的 H200 芯片，只要这些由台湾制造的芯片首先运往美国。信中称，特朗普抵达后加征关税，“通过看似违宪的出口税制度，有效削减了英伟达对中国的销售”。随后，卢特尼克领导下的商务部颁发了出口许可证。
顺便说一句，特朗普和英伟达之间的收入分成协议是公开的。据美联社当时报道，2025 年 8 月，英伟达和 AMD 均同意与美国政府分享其向中国芯片销售收入的 15%，作为获得出口许可证协议的一部分。
但这封信质疑为什么 Lutnick 继续允许 Megaspeed 购买芯片，即使据报道美国情报部门通知他他们对 Alice Huang 以及黄仁勋与她的关系的怀疑。它质疑为什么该部门据报道批准其他亚洲公司购买英伟达芯片，“而这些公司在其列出的地址上没有实体存在”。因此，调查针对的是政府，而不仅仅是英伟达和黄仁勋。
这封信还质疑英伟达对特朗普项目的捐款是如何考虑在内的。信中指出，在特朗普得知黄先生与一名所谓间谍发生关系的“妥协立场”之后，以及英伟达向特朗普的项目（包括舞厅）捐赠了 2600 万美元之后，出口协议才获得批准。这似乎是在询问特朗普是否利用他对此事的了解来获得英伟达的捐款。
有趣的是，在周日播出的特朗普总统的“60 分钟”采访中，他提到他和他的团队如何威胁一名未透露姓名的人工智能高管入狱，之后，这位高管“彻底改变了”。
自涉嫌间谍事件的消息传出以来，国会对英伟达在中国的销售及其与特朗普的交易进行的调查是迄今为止的第二次调查。这个由共和党领导的小组成员包括众议院中国共产党特别委员会、众议院外交事务委员会和众议院情报委员会的领导人。该组织要求黄来找他们并在闭门会议上作证。他们威胁说，如果他不自愿同意，就会传唤他。周四，在他辞职后，他同意了。

title_en: WATCH: Trump administration officials announce PTSD research funding for psychedelic drug ibogaine
title_zh: 观看：特朗普政府官员宣布为迷幻药物伊博加因提供创伤后应激障碍研究资金
summary: Federal officials on Thursday announced new funding to explore the medical potential of ibogaine, a controversial psychedelic drug championed by veterans, conservative lawmakers and podcasters aligned with President Donald Trump.
summary_zh: 联邦官员周四宣布提供新资金，以探索伊博加因的医疗潜力，伊博加因是一种备受争议的迷幻药物，受到退伍军人的拥护
body_en: Matthew Perrone, Associated Press Matthew Perrone, Associated Press
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/watch-trump-administration-officials-announce-ptsd-research-funding-for-psychedelic-drug-ibogaine

WASHINGTON (AP) — Federal officials on Thursday announced new funding to explore the medical potential of ibogaine, a controversial psychedelic drug championed by veterans, conservative lawmakers and podcasters aligned with President Donald Trump.
Watch the news conference in the video player above.

Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said his department is awarding up to $4.9 million to prepare for the first U.S. studies of ibogaine for post-traumatic stress disorder, a hard-to-treat condition linked to higher suicide and substance abuse rates among veterans.
The money will not go directly to patient research, Kennedy said, but to lay the groundwork needed to manufacture, dose and design studies of the drug.
Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

Ibogaine is made from a shrub native to West Africa. It can cause intense hallucinations, nausea, vomiting, tremors and sometimes deadly irregular heart rhythms. Ibogaine is currently illegal, in the same ultra-restrictive class as LSD, ecstasy and most other psychedelic drugs.

Veterans organizations and psychedelic advocates contend that ibogaine has great promise for intractable conditions such as PTSD, severe depression and opioid addiction. U.S. research on the drug has essentially been frozen for decades due to ibogaine's restricted status.

Kennedy said the government will receive data and treatment guidance from Beond Inc., a Texas-based company that has treated more than 3,000 patients with ibogaine in Mexico, where the drug is not illegal.
"That is going to allow us to dramatically accelerate the clinical trial process," Kennedy said. "We're going to have, I think, a record drug approval process."
Additional funding awards may explore ibogaine's use for addiction, he said.
Veterans Affairs Secretary Doug Collins, who joined Kennedy for the announcement, said the collaborative effort would focus first on safety and "best-in-class research."
"For veterans living with PTSD, we owe them both urgency and the best science we can produce," Collins said.

Kennedy and Collins have previously voiced support for the potential of psychedelics, citing the experiences of veterans who have traveled abroad for therapy with ibogaine and other mind-altering substances.

Thursday's announcement was previewed in April, when Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to speed up review and research of psychedelics that could help with mental health conditions.

Three applications for psychedelics are pending review at the Food and Drug Administration. They include the first potential medicines made from psilocybin, the active ingredient in magic mushrooms, and MDMA, also called ecstasy. Decisions on those drugs could come within weeks or months.
Because of its safety risks, ibogaine research has moved more slowly.

The little data currently available mostly comes from patients who have traveled to Mexico or other countries where ibogaine is not heavily regulated. Ibogaine clinics typically charge $10,000 to $20,000 for one course of treatment, which often involves monitoring of a patient's heart readings while emergency medical workers are on standby.
body_zh: 马修·佩罗内，美联社 马修·佩罗内，美联社
华盛顿（美联社）——联邦官员周四宣布提供新资金，用于探索伊博加因的医疗潜力，伊博加因是一种有争议的迷幻药，受到退伍军人、保守派议员和与唐纳德·特朗普总统结盟的播客的支持。
在上面的视频播放器中观看新闻发布会。
卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪 (Robert F. Kennedy Jr.) 表示，他的部门将拨款 490 万美元，为美国首个伊博加因治疗创伤后应激障碍的研究做准备。创伤后应激障碍是一种难以治疗的疾病，与退伍军人较高的自杀率和药物滥用率有关。
肯尼迪说，这笔钱不会直接用于患者研究，而是为该药物的制造、剂量和设计研究奠定必要的基础。
与自由和独立的新闻业站在一起。加入 PBS 新闻的记者通行证
伊博加因是由原产于西非的灌木制成的。它会引起强烈的幻觉、恶心、呕吐、颤抖，有时还会导致致命的心律不齐。伊博加因目前是非法的，与LSD、摇头丸和大多数其他迷幻药物属于同一超限制类别。
退伍军人组织和迷幻药倡导者认为，伊博加因对于治疗创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）、严重抑郁症和阿片类药物成瘾等棘手疾病有很大希望。由于伊博加因的限制地位，美国对该药物的研究基本上被冻结了数十年。
肯尼迪表示，政府将从Beond Inc.获得数据和治疗指导，Beond Inc.是一家总部位于德克萨斯州的公司，该公司已在墨西哥使用伊博加因治疗了3000多名患者，而该药物在墨西哥并不违法。
“这将使我们能够大大加快临床试验进程，”肯尼迪说。 “我认为，我们将拥有创纪录的药物审批流程。”
他说，额外的资金奖励可能会探索伊博加因用于成瘾的用途。
与肯尼迪一起宣布这一消息的退伍军人事务部长道格·柯林斯表示，合作将首先关注安全和“一流的研究”。
柯林斯说：“对于患有创伤后应激障碍 (PTSD) 的退伍军人来说，我们既要紧迫，又要为他们提供最好的科学成果。”
肯尼迪和柯林斯此前曾表示支持迷幻药的潜力，并引用了出国接受伊博加因和其他精神改变药物治疗的退伍军人的经历。
周四的声明在四月份就已被预演，当时特朗普签署了一项行政命令，指示联邦机构加快对有助于治疗心理健康状况的迷幻药的审查和研究。
三份致幻剂申请正在等待美国食品和药物管理局的审查。其中包括第一个由迷幻蘑菇中的活性成分裸盖菇素和摇头丸（也称为摇头丸）制成的潜在药物。关于这些药物的决定可能会在几周或几个月内做出。
由于存在安全风险，伊博加因的研究进展较为缓慢。
目前可用的数据很少，主要来自前往墨西哥或伊博加因不受严格监管的其他国家旅行的患者。伊博加因诊所的一个疗程收费通常为 10,000 至 20,000 美元，通常需要在急救医疗人员待命时监测患者的心脏读数。

title_en: Immigration arrests go on unabated despite Trump's misgivings after the GOP's midterm wipeout
title_zh: 尽管特朗普在共和党中期惨败后心存疑虑，但移民逮捕行动有增无减
summary: In the wake of midterm elections, President Donald Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the Democrats
summary_zh: 中期选举结束后，唐纳德·特朗普总统表示，他的移民镇压可能“过于严厉”，并表示是时候坐下来了
body_en: In the wake of midterm elections, President Donald Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the Democrats
By VALERIE GONZALEZ Associated Press and TIM SULLIVAN Associated Press
It’s business as usual for President Donald Trump's deportation offensive despite the Republican wipeout in the midterm elections.

In Los Angeles, masked immigration officers in body armor blocked a hospital emergency room driveway in a heavily Latino neighborhood early Saturday. In central Alabama, twin 19-year-old brothers from Venezuela were arrested while driving back to college a day after the election.
Advocates reported arrests from California to Michigan to Massachusetts.
After Democrats trounced the GOP and won control of the next Congress, Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the rival party.
“I’d love to do something on immigration,” he said in an interview with CBS “60 Minutes” recorded Friday.

Hours later, he named Stephen Miller, the architect of his hardline immigration agenda, as his new chief of staff. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, meanwhile, said his orders had not changed.

“Deportations will continue,” Mullin wrote in an online post the day after the election, warning that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement takes no days off and that “this includes on Thanksgiving, Christmas, and Election Day.”
María Bilbao, a campaign coordinator for the American Friends Service Committee in Miami, said she has received at least one call a day from someone detained in South Florida since the election.
“Everything remains exactly the same. The arrests have not ceased at all,” Bilbao said.

Florida Highway Patrol officers and ICE agents have detained people in their cars, as well as places including supermarkets, pharmacies and gas stations. Immigrants under supervision have also been arrested when they showed up at ICE's Miami office for their appointments.
Erick Gasca, 31, got home Friday night after an evening playing board games with friends. He lives near Adventist Health White Memorial Medical Center in Los Angeles.
An “unprecedented” number of vehicles with tinted windows and no license plates were parked near the hospital's emergency room entrance, he said.
“I thought they were going to raid the hospital or something,” he recalled.

The Department of Homeland Security declined to explain the officers’ presence there, though Bill Essayli, the top Justice Department prosecutor in Los Angeles, said they were bringing a detainee for medical treatment. Essayli said two people were arrested for assaulting federal agents.
“ICE does not target hospitals, schools, or churches,” DHS said in a statement.
The agents' presence attracted some 30 residents and passersby. Footage shot by Gasca’s cousin, Michelle Rivera, shows protesters shouting and officers pinning someone down.

“White Memorial does not participate in immigration enforcement,” hospital president Daniel Fontoura said in a statement, adding it would not let such activities "compromise our commitment to patient care and safety.”
body_zh: 中期选举结束后，唐纳德·特朗普总统表示，他的移民镇压可能“过于严厉”，并建议是时候与民主党坐下来了
瓦莱丽·冈萨雷斯 (VALERIE GONZALEZ) 美联社和蒂姆·苏利文 (TIM SULLIVAN) 美联社报道
尽管共和党在中期选举中惨败，但唐纳德·特朗普总统的驱逐攻势照常进行。
在洛杉矶，周六早些时候，身着防弹衣的蒙面移民官员封锁了拉丁裔人口密集的社区的一家医院急诊室车道。在阿拉巴马州中部，选举后一天，一对来自委内瑞拉的 19 岁双胞胎兄弟在开车返回大学时被捕。
倡导者报告称，从加利福尼亚州到密歇根州再到马萨诸塞州都有逮捕事件。
在民主党击败共和党并赢得下一届国会的控制权后，特朗普表示他的移民镇压可能“过于严厉”，并建议是时候与对手坐下来了。
“我很乐意在移民问题上做点什么，”他在周五录制的哥伦比亚广播公司“60 分钟”节目中说道。
几个小时后，他任命其强硬移民议程的设计师斯蒂芬·米勒(Stephen Miller)为他的新任幕僚长。与此同时，国土安全部部长马克韦恩·穆林表示，他的命令没有改变。
“驱逐出境将继续，”穆林在选举后第二天在网上发帖写道，警告美国移民和海关执法局没有休息日，“这包括感恩节、圣诞节和选举日。”
迈阿密美国公谊服务委员会的竞选协调员玛丽亚·毕尔巴鄂表示，自大选以来，她每天至少接到一个来自南佛罗里达州被拘留者的电话。
“一切都保持原样。逮捕行动根本没有停止，”毕尔巴鄂说。
佛罗里达州高速公路巡逻人员和 ICE 特工在车内以及超市、药店和加油站等地方拘留了人们。受到监管的移民在前往 ICE 迈阿密办事处赴约时也遭到逮捕。
31 岁的埃里克·加斯卡 (Erick Gasca) 周五晚上与朋友玩了一晚棋盘游戏后回到家。他住在洛杉矶基督复临安息日会怀特纪念医疗中心附近。
他说，医院急诊室入口附近停着数量“史无前例”的有色车窗且没有牌照的车辆。
“我以为他们会突击搜查医院什么的，”他回忆道。
尽管洛杉矶司法部最高检察官比尔·埃萨利 (Bill Essayli) 表示，他们正在带一名被拘留者接受治疗，但国土安全部拒绝解释这些警官的存在。埃萨利说，有两人因袭击联邦特工而被捕。
国土安全部在一份声明中表示：“ICE 不针对医院、学校或教堂。”
特工的出现吸引了大约30名居民和路人。加斯卡的表弟米歇尔·里维拉拍摄的视频显示，抗议者大喊大叫，警察将某人按倒。
医院院长丹尼尔·丰图拉（Daniel Fontoura）在一份声明中表示，“怀特纪念医院不参与移民执法”，并补充说，医院不会让此类活动“损害我们对患者护理和安全的承诺”。

title_en: Trump administration plans to make it harder to get grocery assistance
title_zh: 特朗普政府计划加大获得食品杂货援助的难度
summary: About 6.3 million people could lose eligibility for SNAP by the 2029 fiscal year if the proposed change takes effect, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture. That is on top of 5.5 million people who already have lost SNAP benefits over the past year.
summary_zh: 据美国国务院称，如果拟议的变更生效，到 2029 财年，大约 630 万人可能会失去 SNAP 的资格
body_en: Geoff Mulvihill, Associated Press Geoff Mulvihill, Associated Press

https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/trump-administration-plans-to-make-it-harder-to-get-grocery-assistance
President Donald Trump's administration is planning to make it harder to get food aid through the federal government's big grocery assistance program that serves about 1 in 10 Americans.

The administration says the proposed rule would close a loophole by no longer allowing some people who receive benefits under the federal Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program to automatically qualify for the separate Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program too.

About 6.3 million people could lose eligibility for SNAP by the 2029 fiscal year if the proposed change takes effect, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture, which administers the program. That is on top of 5.5 million people who already have lost SNAP benefits over the past year.

The plan is laid out in a proposed rule published Tuesday on how to run SNAP, and the government is seeking public comment until next month. If it is accepted, the rule would not take full effect for about two years.
The proposal addresses the link between 2 federal programs

At issue are two separate federal programs. The TANF program provides federal grants to states, which set their own eligibility rules for distributing cash and other benefits to low-income families with children. The incomes of recipients vary by program and state.
WATCH: Millions lose SNAP benefits as One Big Beautiful Bill's stricter requirements kick in

Federal guidelines generally limit SNAP food benefits to those earning less than 130% of the poverty level, a little over $1,700 monthly for an individual or nearly $3,600 for a family of four. To reduce duplicative paperwork, the federal government allows people who already receive TANF benefits to automatically qualify for SNAP — though they still have to apply.

Some states have used that automatic eligibility to expand SNAP benefits to people who might not otherwise qualify. In 2009, President Barack Obama's administration encouraged states to provide people a minimal TANF-funded benefit, such as an informational pamphlet or telephone hotline, as a way of qualifying them for the food program.
Forty-one states and the District of Columbia have some form of broad-based categorical eligibility for SNAP, according to a USDA report from last year.
Trump's team put forth a similar plan 7 years ago
The first Trump administration proposed to clamp down on such tactics in 2019. But that proposal was withdrawn by President Joe Biden's administration in 2021.

"Simply put, we did not want to remove millions of people from the program, particularly working poor or children," said Stacy Dean, a former USDA official under Biden who now is executive director of the Global Food Institute at George Washington University.

The latest proposal is more sweeping and could prevent states from basing SNAP eligibility on TANF-funded benefits such as job-related counseling or one-time vouchers for vehicle repairs so that people can get to work, said David Super, a law professor at Georgetown University who has studied the food aid program.
"The administration here is basically proposing to eliminate the flexibility that Congress gave the states to serve working poor people," Super said.

唐纳德·特朗普总统的政府正计划加大通过联邦政府大型杂货援助计划获得粮食援助的难度，该计划为大约十分之一的美国人提供服务。
政府表示，拟议的规则将堵塞一个漏洞，不再允许一些根据联邦贫困家庭临时援助计划领取福利的人自动有资格获得单独的补充营养援助计划。

据管理该计划的美国农业部称，如果拟议的变更生效，到 2029 财年，大约 630 万人可能会失去 SNAP 的资格。除此之外，去年还有 550 万人失去了 SNAP 福利。
该计划包含在周二发布的关于如何运行 SNAP 的拟议规则中，政府正在征求公众意见，直至下个月。如果被接受，该规则将在大约两年内不会完全生效。
该提案解决了两个联邦计划之间的联系
存在争议的是两个独立的联邦计划。 TANF 计划向各州提供联邦拨款，各州制定自己的资格规则，向有孩子的低收入家庭分配现金和其他福利。受益人的收入因计划和州而异。
观看：随着《美丽大法案》更严格的要求生效，数百万人失去了 SNAP 福利
联邦指导方针通常将 SNAP 食品福利限制在那些收入低于贫困线 130% 的人，个人每月略高于 1,700 美元，四口之家接近 3,600 美元。为了减少重复的文书工作，联邦政府允许已经领取 TANF 福利的人自动获得 SNAP 资格——尽管他们仍然需要申请。
一些州利用这种自动资格将 SNAP 福利扩大到原本可能不符合资格的人。 2009年，巴拉克·奥巴马总统的政府鼓励各州向人们提供最低限度的贫困家庭临时援助（TANF）资助的福利，例如信息小册子或电话热线，作为使他们有资格参加粮食计划的一种方式。
根据美国农业部去年的一份报告，四十一个州和哥伦比亚特区拥有某种形式的 SNAP 基础广泛的分类资格。
特朗普团队7年前就提出过类似计划
第一届特朗普政府于 2019 年提议打击此类策略。但该提议于 2021 年被乔·拜登总统的政府撤回。
拜登领导下的前美国农业部官员、现任乔治华盛顿大学全球食品研究所执行主任史黛西·迪恩 (Stacy Dean) 表示：“简而言之，我们不想让数百万人退出该计划，特别是贫困工人或儿童。”
乔治城大学研究食品援助计划的法学教授戴维·苏佩尔 (David Super) 表示，最新的提案更为全面，可能会阻止各州将 SNAP 资格建立在贫困家庭临时援助 (TANF) 资助的福利上，例如与工作相关的咨询或车辆维修的一次性代金券，以便人们能够上班。
超级说：“政府基本上是提议取消国会赋予各州为贫困工人服务的灵活性。”
